summary: Judge panel: four independent project designs, three lens judges, synthesis, adversarial critic

designs.name: LabSleuth: teaching an on-device vision-language model to diagnose lab errors, with a physics simulator as its only teacher (continuation of Physics Pictorial Recognition)
designs.one_line_pitch: Physics is the only teacher. A 9B vision-language model that runs on a laptop is LoRA-trained on about 10k simulator-generated lab notebooks with injected systematic errors, each graded by an exact Bayesian referee. It learns to name the error in a student's data and the one measurement that would prove it. Against levelled baselines, we test whether that skill transfers to experiments it never saw. Everything runs offline, inside the 24 GB cap, with no API.
designs.research_question: Does LoRA fine-tuning a 9-billion-parameter on-device vision-language model only on physics-simulator lab data with injected systematic errors, labelled by an exact Bayesian referee, make it better at identifying the systematic error and choosing the most discriminating next measurement in school physics experiments it never saw in training than the same untuned model, its untuned 27-billion-parameter sibling and frontier API models given identical prompts, tools and output schema?
hypotheses_or_criteria: H1 (primary, transfer). Test set: L3a, 6 held-out experiment families, with the law, candidate causes and action menu given. Claim: adapted-9B beats untuned-9B on top-1 cause accuracy on identifiable items by >= 8 percentage points (exact McNemar, two-sided p < 0.05). Both get the same prompt contract, signature panel, JSON schema, greedy decoding and 512-token budget.

H2 (small specialist vs big generalist). Adapted-9B is non-inferior to untuned Qwen3.8-27B on L3a: the lower bound of the 95% CI of the paired difference is > -3 pp. It also uses <= 50% of the 27B's peak memory and <= 50% of its median time-to-answer on the same Mac. Judged on the server; re-checked on the Mac parity subset, where both models run 4-bit.

H3 (do no harm). Test data: simulated with no systematic error. A false alarm is adapted-9B giving p(no error) < 0.5 while the referee gives >= 0.8. Claim: the false-alarm rate is <= 10% (Wilson 95% upper bound <= 15%) and lower than untuned-9B's (McNemar).

H4 (experimental design). Adapted-9B's normalized EIG regret on its next-measurement choice is lower than untuned-9B's (Wilcoxon signed-rank, p < 0.05). Its closed-loop success within two extra measurements is >= 10 pp higher (McNemar).

H5 (faithfulness). A violation is an explanation containing a number, unit, verdict or cause ID that contradicts the computed panel. Before the checker gate, adapted-9B's violation rate is <= 3% and lower than untuned-9B's (McNemar). After the gate, displayed violations are <= 1%.

H6 (what the upgrade must NOT change). Photo-based experiment recognition on the public open-set image set (plus the 809-image set if the SRC allows) changes by less than +/-5 pp. A fixed 300-item general physics set changes by less than +/-3 pp. Equivalence means the 90% CI of the paired difference lies inside the margin.

H7 (negative control, P1). A LoRA trained on the same episodes, with cause labels shuffled within each family, improves L3a accuracy by < 2 pp over untuned-9B. This shows that any H1 gain comes from the physics-verified labels, not from exposure to the output format.

Engineering criteria (deployment): (a) the Mac MLX 4-bit base with the converted adapter stays within 3 pp of the server bf16 adapter on the 300-item parity set; (b) the whole product stack peaks at <= 12 GB, well under the 24 GB cap; (c) median diagnosis time <= 15 s; (d) recognition <= 10 s for a photo of <= 1024 px; (e) 100% offline.

Exploratory, with no confirmatory claim: (a) accuracy on the student's own controlled real measurements with deliberately set conditions, reported with exact Clopper-Pearson intervals; (b) learning-curve checkpoints; (c) near- vs far-transfer breakdown by held-out cause.

Rule for all of the above: the student restates every hypothesis and acceptance line in his own words and fixes the numbers in the signed research plan before any data generation, training or evaluation. Eval-set hashes are appended to the plan before training. Each arm has one pre-specified checkpoint. A miss is reported as a miss.
designs.product_experience:
STUDENT (Chinese or English interface, fully offline)
(1) Pick one of the six curriculum experiments from the list (manual selection stays), or upload a setup photo.
(2) Photo path:
- YOLOv8s boxes the apparatus and the student corrects the boxes on the existing canvas.
- The same local 9B model (its vision is unchanged by the upgrade) sees the photo with numbered marks. It returns a candidate set over the six curriculum experiments plus 'other: <name>'.
- If the set holds more than one experiment (the proven cart+track tie), it asks ONE yes/no question chosen to split the set, e.g. 'Is a weight hanging from a string over a pulley?'.
- For 'other', it drafts an experiment card: law as a formula, variables, units, candidate errors and possible measurements. Nothing is computed until the card passes a unit/formula check and the student confirms it.
(3) Optional predict step: the student taps whether they expect agreement with the ideal law and which error they suspect. This is stored locally only (the predict-before-feedback teaching method).
(4) Data entry: a multi-trial table is generated from the card.
- One row is allowed, but the app nudges for repeats and a varied independent variable.
- Instrument resolutions (e.g. the spring-scale division) are pre-filled and editable.
(5) Result card: the physical quantity with an uncertainty budget (resolution d/sqrt(12), ruler +/-1 mm, manual timing sigma about 0.10 s). A z-score consistency verdict replaces the old fixed '<15% = verified' rule.
(6) Detective card:
- Ranked causes with probabilities and the data signature behind each. Example: 'friction not compensated 0.71 - your a-vs-m line has a negative intercept; hanging mass not << cart mass 0.21 - slight downward bend; no error 0.03'.
- ONE next measurement, with what to expect under each of the top two causes.
- A counterfactual plot: the student's points overlaid on the curve each cause would produce.
(7) Closed loop:
- The student takes that measurement and adds a row; the probabilities update, for up to three rounds.
- Final card: the most likely cause, and how to reduce it (the curriculum's 'analyse errors and propose ways to reduce them').
- A short explanation follows. Every number in it is checked against the computed panel; on failure it is regenerated once, otherwise a template is shown.
(8) The existing idealized animation now overlays measured vs ideal.

Who decides:
- Curriculum experiments: the exact Bayesian referee supplies the probabilities and the fine-tuned model writes the explanation. Its own diagnosis is cross-checked, and the referee wins any disagreement.
- Any other experiment: the fine-tuned model's diagnosis is shown, labelled 'model estimate'.

TEACHER
(1) Before class: choose the lesson's experiments and set the real instruments once (division values, stopwatch or photogate, cart mass, track length).
(2) P1: ask the model to draft a card for a non-curriculum experiment, then edit and approve it. The card's errors are expressed as generic error patterns, so it becomes a registry entry run by the exact referee: the model proposes, physics verifies, the teacher approves.
(3) In class: 'classroom mode' shows only referee results and checked templates, never free-generated text. The teacher can project a group's table to discuss causes.
(4) After class: an optional local export of anonymous cause counts. This is a product feature only, never collected as research data without IRB approval.

JUDGES AT THE BOOTH (English, frozen offline build)
- 'Beat the detective': the judge secretly picks an experiment and a fault in the simulator. LabSleuth sees only the generated readings and must name the cause within two extra measurements.
- The photo path, run on the student's own apparatus photos.

technical_components.name: C1 LabSim + LabFault-24 data generator
technical_components.what:
Declarative library of 24 experiment families.
- Each family: ideal law (sympy) + design ranges + instruments (resolution, noise) + 3-4 systematic errors.
- Errors are drawn from a shared library of error patterns: additive offset, gain/calibration, time offset, resistive loss, neglected mass or inertia, approximation breakdown, wrong reference length, threshold nonlinearity, drift. Each is bound to a family-specific physical cause, data signature, fix and action menu.
- Training families (18): the six curriculum experiments (friction, average speed on an incline, Hooke, Newton-2 with hanging mass, momentum with two carts, energy on an incline) plus free fall, incline acceleration, projectile from a table, spring-mass oscillation, centripetal force, buoyancy, density by displacement, collision restitution, Ohm's law, Snell's law, Boyle's law, resonance tube.
- Held-out families (6, never in training): pendulum period, Atwood machine, lever balance, thin-lens equation, calorimetry, cell internal resistance.
- Priors from verified literature: manual start-stop timing N(0, 0.10^2 s^2); single-action bias 0.11 s, sd 0.07 s; resolution d/sqrt(12); ruler +/-1 mm; Newton-2 approximation error (m+m_e)/M; photogate bias about 5.7%; omitted rotational KE; rolling-plus-sliding ball in the collision apparatus; tilted or unsteady pulls in the friction experiment. Student pendulum g spread (sd 0.28 m/s^2) is a validation target. Anything without a literature value is tagged 'assumption' and randomized.
- Episodes: 1-10 trials (25% single-trial, like today's classes); readings rounded to instrument resolution; 25% no-error; Chinese/English 50/50; 20% messy input (unit slips, missing units); randomized cause IDs and order; three paraphrases per text slot.
- Deterministic seeds plus a SHA-256 manifest, so the dataset can be regenerated anywhere from code.
technical_components.novelty_vs_prior_art: Simulator-generated physics training data exists (Sim2Reason: MuJoCo QA with a 5%-tolerance reward; PhysEvolve; Mind's Eye), but for problem solving or visual prediction. Not found anywhere: measurement-level fault injection with literature-calibrated noise for school experiments, labelled with exact posteriors and EIG.
technical_components.feasibility_and_memory: numpy + sympy, CPU only, < 1 GB RAM. About 1.5-2k lines (estimate), written by the AI assistant before 11-06 and checked with seconds-long unit tests on the Mac. Tens of thousands of episodes generate in minutes on the server CPUs (estimate).

technical_components.name: C2 Exact Bayesian referee (teacher, judge and in-product engine)
technical_components.what:
- Posterior over {no error, error_1..k}, with each error magnitude marginalised on a 1-D grid under the known noise model (model discrimination).
- Expected information gain of each menu action, by Monte Carlo with about 256 simulated outcomes per action.
- Identifiability flag: posterior of the true cause >= 0.6 (threshold pre-registered).
- An uncertainty-normalised z verdict that replaces physics.py's fixed 15% rule.
- Three uses: it labels the SFT data, scores every arm, and runs exactly in the product for registry experiments.
technical_components.novelty_vs_prior_art: The methods are classic: Box & Hill 1967 model discrimination, de Kleer & Williams 1987 entropy-minimising next measurement, modern Bayesian optimal experimental design. Blais 2020 brought model comparison to intro labs. What is new is only the use: a parametric school-lab error library with EIG advice, serving as a verifiable teacher for a language model.
technical_components.feasibility_and_memory: Vectorised numpy, about 10-50 ms per episode (estimate), negligible memory. Runs on the Mac inside the product.

technical_components.name: C3 Shared signature panel (levelling tool)
technical_components.what:
Generic statistics computed from law plus table for any family, and given identically to every arm:
- per-trial residual z and chi^2/dof against the ideal law
- fitted slope and intercept with uncertainties, and the slope ratio to ideal
- curvature-term z
- repeat scatter against the expected sigma
- trial-order drift
- before/after ratios for conservation families
This takes arithmetic out of the comparison, so a gain cannot be 'the fine-tune learned to compute'. A no-panel ablation measures what the tool itself contributes.
technical_components.novelty_vs_prior_art: Standard statistics in a tool-integrated-reasoning pattern (PAL, ToRA). Not claimed as new.
technical_components.feasibility_and_memory: numpy, milliseconds.

technical_components.name: C4 Lab-diagnosis LoRA on Qwen3.5-9B (the centerpiece upgrade)
technical_components.what:
- Adapter: bf16 LoRA, r=16, alpha=32, dropout 0.05.
- Targets: the language model's linear layers (full-attention q/k/v/o, Gated-DeltaNet in_proj_qkv/in_proj_z/out_proj, MLP gate/up/down). Vision tower, embeddings and lm_head stay frozen.
- Format: non-thinking chat format; loss on assistant tokens only.
- Data: 6-10k episodes from the 18 training families. In 6 of them one error is withheld for the L2 test and also removed from their training candidate lists, so it never appears as a distractor that is never correct.
- Time box: <= 4 h or 2 epochs, whichever comes first.
- Target: a fixed JSON with the referee posterior rounded to 0.05, the EIG-best action with the expected direction of change under the top two causes, a fix ID, the z verdict, and a <= 80-word bilingual templated explanation.
technical_components.novelty_vs_prior_art: Rejection-sampling fine-tuning, STaR and RLVR exist, and so do simulator rewards (Sim2Reason, but for problem solving). New here: (1) the task, posterior-calibrated diagnosis plus measurement design from noisy measurements; (2) a physics engine as the only teacher, with no human labels and no API teacher; (3) an explicit held-out-family transfer test. LLMs are documented to be weak exactly here: EIG-style design in BoxingGym; 0.60 on controlled-experiment judgement (Bewersdorff 2023); lab-assistant replies wrong or harmful about 1 in 10 (Kregear 2025) to 1 in 5 (Maus 2025).
technical_components.feasibility_and_memory: Unsloth's Qwen3.5 table gives about 22 GB VRAM for 9B bf16 LoRA, inside the RTX 5090's 32 GB. That table does not state a sequence length, so verify in the first run. This route also avoids Unsloth's warning against QLoRA for this family. The adapter is about 87 MB. Throughput is measured in the first 10 minutes and the episode count is set to fit the 4-h box.

technical_components.name: C5 Levelled, pre-registered evaluation harness
technical_components.what:
- Frozen eval sets, with hashes in the plan before training.
- One contract prompt and identical inputs for all arms: card, table, panel, candidate list, menu.
- Decoding: JSON-schema-constrained where supported, greedy, 512 new tokens, thinking off for local arms.
- Automatic verifier: cause accuracy on identifiable items, error-pattern accuracy, Brier, ECE, false alarms, EIG regret, expected-outcome direction, and a faithfulness checker for numbers, units, verdicts and IDs.
- Statistics module: exact McNemar, Wilcoxon, Wilson, Clopper-Pearson, cluster bootstrap by family, mixed-effects logistic regression, Holm.
- Positive controls: an arm with the oracle answer in the prompt must score about 100%; a planted large-error set; a planted duplicate that the leakage checker must catch; an adapter-effect check after conversion.
technical_components.novelty_vs_prior_art: The method follows the student's reference paper (Gewu): acceptance lines written before runs, baselines levelled on grader, budget, tool and prompt, and positive controls. New is the capability ladder for lab diagnosis.
technical_components.feasibility_and_memory:
- Server, local arms: vLLM batches them on the 5090 (its Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration implementation handles LoRA); HF transformers is the fallback.
- Server, 27B: llama.cpp with the GGUF build.
- Mac checks: mlx_vlm.server.

technical_components.name: C6 Mac deployment within the 24 GB cap
technical_components.what:
- PEFT-to-MLX adapter converter: rename keys; transpose PEFT lora_A/lora_B into mlx-vlm's lora_a (in,r) / lora_b (r,out); set scale = alpha/r.
- Serving: mlx_vlm.server --adapter-path on the lmstudio-community Qwen3.5-9B MLX 4-bit base. It has thinking off by default, JSON schema with images, and logprobs.
- Fallback, because LM Studio cannot load adapters: merge on the server -> GGUF Q4_K_M -> private Hugging Face repo -> Mac -> LM Studio with the base mmproj.
- Memory guard: sums the footprint of our processes every 5 s; above 22.5 GB it stops the eval client first, then Streamlit, then YOLO, then the model server.
technical_components.novelty_vs_prior_art: Engineering. The parity test with an adapter-effect positive control is a small reusable contribution.
technical_components.feasibility_and_memory: Estimated product stack about 8-10 GB, to be measured on 11-09: 5.98 GB weights + about 0.09 GB adapter + about 1-2 GB KV and vision transients at 8k context and <= 1024 px + about 1-1.5 GB for Streamlit, YOLOv8s and the referee (all estimates). Never co-resident with the 27B: together about 27-29 GB.

technical_components.name: C7 Product integration: the closed-loop lab detective
technical_components.what:
Code snapshot read: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-billgao-Documents-Coding-SCPKU-Proj/8ddfdf88-0966-42bf-b144-14b773fe7f66/scratchpad/repo/src/
- Registry v2, shared with LabSim (multi-trial tables, instruments, errors, fixes, actions), replaces physics.py's single-reading forms.
- New outputs: z verdict, detective card, next-measurement loop, counterfactual overlay plot.
- Faithfulness gate: one regeneration, then template fallback.
- Modes: classroom mode (referee + templates only) and an English mode for judges.
- Local only: explain_api.py (GLM/zhipuai) is removed; a local client talks to mlx_vlm.server or LM Studio.
- intent_classifier.py keeps its rules and manual selection, with the local VLM replacing the GLM fallback.
technical_components.novelty_vs_prior_art: PhysicsAssistant (YOLOv8 + GPT-3.5, 8th-grade labs) is nearly isomorphic to the current app and does perception plus chat only. The new product layer is closed-loop error diagnosis on the student's own numbers.
technical_components.feasibility_and_memory: Streamlit on the Mac, < 1 GB. Code only before 11-06.

technical_components.name: C8 Verifier-filtered self-training + controls
technical_components.what:
- Sampling: 4 answers (temperature 0.8) per episode from the SFT adapter, on 3k fresh training-family episodes, using vLLM+LoRA.
- Filter: keep the best answer that passes the verifier (correct cause on identifiable items, EIG regret <= 0.2, faithfulness pass, valid JSON).
- Then 1 more epoch on the accepted set (about 2-2.5k, estimate).
- Controls on the same items: shuffled-label LoRA, 3-shot in-context baseline, no-panel ablation, learning-curve checkpoints.
technical_components.novelty_vs_prior_art: Expert iteration in the RFT (Yuan 2023) / STaR (Zelikman 2022) style. It is done offline rather than as online GRPO because Unsloth's Qwen3.5 RL workflow cannot use vLLM fast inference.
technical_components.feasibility_and_memory: About 1.5-2.5 GPU-hours (estimate). The control LoRA takes about 3-4 h and runs overnight.

technical_components.name: C9 Open-set path: set-valued recognition, one clarifying question, experiment cards
technical_components.what:
- Set-of-Mark prompt: numbered YOLO boxes drawn on a <= 1024 px photo; the model returns a set over the six curriculum experiments plus 'other: <name>'.
- Split-conformal 90% sets from token logprobs (mlx_vlm.server and vLLM both expose them).
- When the set holds several curriculum experiments, the app asks the single yes/no question with the highest expected information gain over the set.
- For 'other', the model writes an experiment card. Its law must parse in sympy and pass a dimensional check. For LabSim held-out families it must also match the true law numerically on random inputs (this is the L3b test).
technical_components.novelty_vs_prior_art: Conformal sets for zero-shot VLMs (CVPR 2025) and asking when a request is ambiguous (CLAM) both exist; neither was found for experiment-type recognition. The card checks resemble work where an LLM writes a physics program (LLMPhy, PAL).
technical_components.feasibility_and_memory: Inference only. A 1024 px image is about 1,024 visual tokens.

technical_components.name: C10 School-laptop 4B tier and family cross-validation
technical_components.what:
- 4B tier: the same recipe on Qwen3.5-4B (bf16 LoRA about 10 GB VRAM; MLX 4-bit 3.06 GB; adapter about 65 MB) for 8 GB school laptops.
- Cross-validation: 3 folds over the 18 non-curriculum families, each fold holding out 6, so H1 is tested on 18 held-out families instead of 6.
technical_components.novelty_vs_prior_art: Scaling evidence and family-level generalization.
technical_components.feasibility_and_memory: The 4B run takes about 1-2 h; each extra 9B fold about 3-4 h (estimates). Run only if the GPU is free by 11-08; otherwise it is a phase listed in the plan for after 11-15.

technical_components.name: C11 GRPO pilot and 27B QLoRA replication
technical_components.what:
- A short GRPO run on the 4B, with reward = cause correctness + (1 - Brier) + (1 - EIG regret) + faithfulness.
- A 27B QLoRA run (Unsloth says it fits 24 GB) to see whether the recipe also helps the big model. Mac quality is re-validated after merging and re-quantizing.
technical_components.novelty_vs_prior_art: Tests whether online RL adds anything over RFT. Risky.
technical_components.feasibility_and_memory: Slow, because generation inside the RL loop runs through HF. After 11-15 unless time is left.

technical_components.name: C12 Visual counterfactual minimal pairs
technical_components.what: Using the YOLO boxes of the 809 images, inpaint (classical OpenCV, CPU) either the decisive apparatus (hanging weight, dynamometer, second cart) or an irrelevant region with the same artefact. Recognition should change only in the first case. This tests whether the VLM reads the configuration or just the list of objects.
technical_components.novelty_vs_prior_art: Equipment-level minimal-pair tests of VLMs for lab setups were not found. Winoground, MMVP and NaturalBench are general-purpose.
technical_components.feasibility_and_memory: Minutes on the CPU; the boxes already exist. Evaluation only.

designs.model_upgrade:
WHAT IS MODIFIED
The language side of an on-device vision-language model: Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B. It is official, Apache-2.0, natively takes images and video, and has the same qwen3_5 hybrid Gated-DeltaNet architecture as the student's Qwen3.8-27B.
- Method: a bf16 LoRA adapter (r=16, alpha=32, dropout 0.05).
- Targets: full-attention q/k/v/o, Gated-DeltaNet in_proj_qkv/in_proj_z/out_proj, MLP gate/up/down.
- Frozen: vision tower, embeddings, lm_head.

SKILL TAUGHT
Input: an experiment card (law, variables, instruments), a multi-trial table and the shared signature panel. Output, in a fixed JSON contract:
- a calibrated posterior over candidate systematic errors, including 'no error'
- the most informative next measurement, with the expected direction of change under the top two causes
- a fix
- a z verdict
- an explanation of <= 80 words, in Chinese or English

DATA
LabFault-24 episodes, generated by code on the rented RTX 5090 (nothing is uploaded except code) and labelled by the exact Bayesian referee. No human labels, no API teacher, no student data in training.

TRAINING
- Stage 1 (P0): SFT on 6-10k episodes from 18 families; time-boxed to <= 4 h or 2 epochs; non-thinking chat format; loss on assistant tokens. Tool: Unsloth, falling back to ms-swift, then PEFT+TRL.
- Stage 2 (P1): verifier-filtered self-training. Sample 4 answers per fresh episode with vLLM+LoRA, keep the best verified one, and train one more epoch.
- Controls: shuffled-label LoRA, 3-shot in-context baseline, no-panel ablation.

COMPUTE
- RTX 5090, 32 GB. bf16 LoRA needs about 22 GB per Unsloth's Qwen3.5 table (verify at our sequence length).
- Evaluation with vLLM, whose Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration class handles LoRA.
- 27B baseline with llama.cpp, GGUF Q4_K_M.
- Unsloth's Qwen3.5 guide says vLLM fast inference is not supported for RL, which is why Stage 2 is offline RFT rather than online GRPO.
- Checked today: [vLLM qwen3_5 docs](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/stable/api/vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_5/), [Unsloth Qwen3.5 fine-tune](https://unsloth.ai/docs/jp/moderu/qwen3.5/fine-tune), [NeMo RL Qwen3.5](https://docs.nvidia.com/nemo/rl/nightly/guides/models/qwen/qwen3-5.html).

DEPLOYMENT
- The adapter (about 87 MB) goes server -> private HF repo -> Mac.
- A PEFT-to-MLX converter handles key renaming, the A/B transpose and scale = alpha/r.
- It is served by mlx_vlm.server --adapter-path on the 5.98 GB MLX 4-bit base, with thinking off, JSON schema and logprobs. This route is needed because LM Studio cannot load adapters.
- Fallback: merge -> GGUF Q4_K_M -> LM Studio.
- Product stack is about 8-10 GB (estimate). The 27B is swapped in only as a baseline or an optional second opinion.

HOW IT IS MEASURED
The E1-E8 ladder:
- What it should change: cause accuracy on known, noise-shifted, withheld and unseen families; EIG regret and closed-loop success; calibration and false alarms; faithfulness.
- What it should not change: photo recognition and general accuracy. Arithmetic is levelled out by the panel.
- Deployment: Mac-vs-server parity, memory and latency.

WHY THE 9B, NOT THE 27B
- On 32 GB only a 27B QLoRA fits. Unsloth advises against QLoRA for Qwen3.5, and transfer from bnb-NF4 training to MLX-affine serving is untested.
- The 27B alone already takes 18.5-21 GB of the 24 GB cap.
- 'Specialist 9B vs generalist 27B on the same laptop' becomes a headline test instead (H2). A 27B QLoRA replication is P2.

CONSIDERED AND NOT ADOPTED
- Fine-tuning recognition on the 809 photos: they have no experiment-type labels, and 568 of them are frames of 3 source videos, so leakage and few distinct setups.
- Distilling an API teacher: API models are baseline-only.
- Online GRPO in P0: it would be slow (see COMPUTE).
- Photoreal rendering: Blender/Kubric is too costly before 11-09.
- Letting the VLM read gauges: MeasureBench's best model reaches 30.3% on real images, so readings stay manual.

experiments.name: E1 Diagnosis ladder: what the upgrade changes (primary)
experiments.data:
Frozen LabFault-24 sets:
- L1: the 18 training families with new seeds (1,200).
- L1-shift: the same families with heavier-tailed noise (Student t, nu=3), doubled timing noise and coarser resolution (600).
- L2: the 6 withheld family-error pairs (600).
- L3a: the 6 held-out families, with law, candidate causes and menu given (900).
- L3b (P1): held-out families where the model must first write the law (300).
experiments.arms_and_baselines:
Every arm gets the same contract, panel, schema, decoding and budget.
- Bayesian referee: the ceiling (it has exact likelihoods even for held-out families).
- Classical ML on panel features: gradient-boosted trees with error-pattern-level labels only, to answer 'is a language model needed at all?'.
- Untuned Qwen3.5-9B, and untuned 9B with 3 in-context examples.
- Untuned Qwen3.8-27B, non-thinking: GGUF Q4_K_M on the server, plus an MLX parity subset on the Mac.
- 27B with thinking at reasoning effort 'low', 2,048-token budget (P1, 300 items).
- 2-3 frontier API models, precomputed on 100 L1 + 200 L3a items.
- Adapted 9B after SFT, and after SFT+RFT (P1).
- Shuffled-label 9B (P1).
- Adapted 4B (P1).
experiments.metrics_and_stats:
- Primary: top-1 cause accuracy on identifiable L3a items, adapted vs untuned 9B, exact McNemar.
- Secondary: the same on L1, L1-shift and L2; error-pattern-level accuracy for all arms; macro-F1; Brier; share of the referee's accuracy reached; per-family and near- vs far-transfer breakdown; non-inferiority CI against the 27B (H2).
- Family-level uncertainty: cluster bootstrap over families (10,000 resamples) and mixed-effects logistic regression with a family random intercept.
- Holm correction across the secondary tests.
experiments.sample_size: L3a has 900 items, about 550-630 of them identifiable (estimate). About 300-400 paired items give 80-90% power to detect +8 pp at 25% discordance (standard McNemar approximation, estimate). About 3,300 E1 items per local arm (3,600 with L3b); 300 per API arm.
experiments.human_participants_status: None: simulator data only. No IRB needed.

experiments.name: E2 Next-measurement design and closed-loop episodes
experiments.data:
- 600 single-step items (300 L1, 300 L3a), each with a menu of 4-6 actions.
- 300 closed-loop episodes: the simulator hides the true cause and executes the chosen measurement, for up to two extra rounds.
experiments.arms_and_baselines:
- EIG-optimal policy (ceiling) and random policy (floor), both with the referee's diagnosis.
- Untuned 9B, 9B with 3 in-context examples, untuned 27B.
- API models (100 single-step items).
- Adapted 9B after SFT and after SFT+RFT.
experiments.metrics_and_stats:
- Normalized EIG regret (Wilcoxon signed-rank).
- Correctness of the predicted direction of change under the top two causes.
- Closed-loop success: final cause correct, on episodes the oracle policy can solve (McNemar).
- Policy-only success: the model's measurements plus the referee's diagnosis. This separates choosing a measurement from drawing the conclusion.
- Mean rounds; bootstrap CIs.
experiments.sample_size: 600 single-step items + 300 episodes (up to 900 model calls) per local arm.
experiments.human_participants_status: None.

experiments.name: E3 Calibration, abstention and false alarms
experiments.data:
- All E1 items.
- The no-error subset: about 25% of every set, >= 300 items in L1+L3a.
- A 300-item calibration split from the L1 distribution, for conformal sets.
experiments.arms_and_baselines: As in E1: all local arms; API arms on their subset.
experiments.metrics_and_stats:
- Brier, ECE (15 bins), negative log-likelihood.
- False-alarm rate on no-error data (Wilson CI, McNemar).
- Correct 'not enough data - measure X' answers on non-identifiable items.
- P1: split-conformal 90% coverage and mean set size on the L1 test set vs L3a. This measures coverage under family shift, and is reported as is if it drops.
experiments.sample_size: >= 300 no-error items; 300 calibration items plus the E1 test sets.
experiments.human_participants_status: None.

experiments.name: E4 Faithfulness of explanations
experiments.data:
- Every E1/E2 output.
- 120 random paired explanations (untuned vs adapted), in random order with the arm hidden.
experiments.arms_and_baselines: Untuned 9B, untuned 27B, API, adapted SFT, adapted SFT+RFT, each with and without the checker gate.
experiments.metrics_and_stats:
- Violation rate before the gate. A violation is: a number not in the panel within rounding, a wrong unit, a verdict that contradicts z, a nonexistent cause ID, or a fix that does not match the stated cause.
- Displayed violations after the gate and fallback.
- The student's blinded three-level rating (correct / minor issue / wrong). Limitation: the rater is the researcher.
- McNemar and Wilson CIs.
experiments.sample_size: About 4,000 automatically checked outputs per arm; 120 rated pairs.
experiments.human_participants_status: None: the researcher rates machine outputs; no other person is involved.

experiments.name: E5 What the upgrade must NOT change
experiments.data:
- (a) Public open-set image set, test-only: about 150-300 Commons photos plus keyframes from topic-labelled CC BY 3.0 (Getaclass) and CC BY-SA 4.0 (Physics Wikiexperiments) video lessons. Labels are verified by the student; licences are kept in a manifest.
- (b) The 809 annotated images, grouped by source (241 photos, frames of 3 source videos), only if the SRC accepts them as this project's data.
- (c) A fixed 300-item subset of PhyX (MIT licence), with images.
experiments.arms_and_baselines: Untuned vs adapted 9B with identical prompts; untuned 27B as a reference.
experiments.metrics_and_stats:
- Top-1 recognition on canonical experiment names.
- Known-vs-unknown AUROC from logprobs.
- Accuracy on the general set.
- Equivalence (TOST): the 90% CI of the paired difference lies within +/-5 pp for recognition and +/-3 pp for the general set.
- Latency vs image size (512 / 768 / 1024 px).
experiments.sample_size: 150-300 open-set images (plus the 809 if allowed); 300 general items.
experiments.human_participants_status: None: licensed public images and the student's own apparatus photos. Check for identifiable people first, crop or blur, and never display such images without releases.

experiments.name: E6 Controls and ablations: why it changes
experiments.data: The frozen L3a (900) and L1 (1,200) items.
experiments.arms_and_baselines:
- Shuffled-label LoRA (P1).
- 3-shot in-context learning.
- No panel (raw table only), for both untuned and adapted.
- Template-only SFT vs SFT+RFT (P1).
- Learning-curve checkpoints.
- r=16 vs r=32 (P2).
experiments.metrics_and_stats: Same metrics as E1. Exact McNemar against the untuned model and against the adapted model. Checkpoints are exploratory only.
experiments.sample_size: The same frozen items as E1.
experiments.human_participants_status: None.

experiments.name: E7 Deployment fidelity and efficiency on the Mac
experiments.data:
- A 300-item parity set (200 L1 + 100 L3a).
- 50 timed runs per scenario: recognition, diagnosis, one closed-loop round.
experiments.arms_and_baselines:
- Server bf16 adapter (the reference).
- Mac MLX 4-bit base with the converted adapter.
- Fallback GGUF Q4_K_M in LM Studio.
- Untuned 9B and untuned 27B on the same Mac, for latency and memory.
experiments.metrics_and_stats:
- Top-1 agreement and accuracy difference (McNemar, bootstrap CI).
- Adapter-effect positive control: the converted adapter must differ from the base wherever the server adapter does.
- Peak summed footprint, median and IQR time-to-answer, output tokens.
experiments.sample_size: 300 items; 50 timed runs per scenario.
experiments.human_participants_status: None: the student is the only tester.

experiments.name: E8 Sim-to-real pilot on the student's own measurements
experiments.data:
Tables the student records himself, with deliberately set conditions, for example:
- Newton-2 with and without friction compensation, and with a heavy hanging mass.
- Hooke with a spring scale that is not zeroed.
- Friction with an angled pull.
- Incline timing over short distances.
- Careful no-error runs.
All data are entered before any model is run. No photos are needed and no names are recorded.
experiments.arms_and_baselines: Referee, untuned 9B, adapted 9B, untuned 27B, API (precomputed).
experiments.metrics_and_stats: Top-1 cause against the intended condition, agreement with the referee, and false alarms on the careful runs. Clopper-Pearson CIs. Descriptive and exploratory only.
experiments.sample_size: >= 12 datasets of 5-8 trials each by 11-14, if the lab is available; otherwise none before 11-15. Target >= 36 by February, under the same signed protocol.
experiments.human_participants_status: Exempt: the student researcher alone measures and tests, and no human variable is studied. Timing offsets are introduced procedurally (e.g. starting the stopwatch at a marked later point), not by studying his reaction time. Confirm with the SRC.

designs.data_plan:
Everything the model is trained on is generated by code on the rented RTX 5090. Only code crosses the 100 KB/s upload.

(1) LabFault-24, generated by 'labsim generate' from fixed seeds:
- Training: 6-10k episodes from 18 families, balanced by family and cause; 25% no-error, 25% single-trial; Chinese/English 50/50; 20% messy input.
- A 300-item validation set from the training families, for sanity checks only.
- Frozen eval sets: L1 1,200; L1-shift 600; L2 600; L3a 900; L3b 300; E2 600 items + 300 episodes; calibration 300; positive controls 100.
- Held-out families and withheld family-error pairs never appear in training data or in training candidate lists.
- Seeds and SHA-256 hashes are appended to the signed plan before training.

(2) Priors: every noise or magnitude prior is tagged with its literature source or as 'assumption'. The student signs off on the six curriculum families.

(3) Real data: E8 tables typed by the student into CSV (kilobytes, no names), kept and evaluated on the Mac.

(4) Images, test-only, never trained on:
- dataset.zip is pulled by the server straight from the public GitHub repo (809 images + YOLO labels). It is used for E5b/C12 only if the SRC agrees.
- The open-set set is harvested through the Commons API: standard thumbnail sizes, <= 2 parallel downloads, a contact User-Agent, sha1 de-duplication. A manifest records title, author, URL and licence. Titles give candidate labels only; the student verifies each one.
- The 25-photo intent set from the earlier classroom sessions is not used as ISEF evidence unless the SRC confirms it may be.
- About 5 of the ~65 images already on the Mac serve only for the optional dry-run probe.

(5) General set: 300 fixed PhyX items, pulled on the server.

(6) No frontier-API output is ever used as training data. API answers exist only as precomputed baselines.

(7) Storage (estimates): server >= 100 GB (9B bf16 about 19 GB, 4B about 9 GB, 27B GGUF about 18 GB, checkpoints about 1 GB). Mac: models about 22 GB plus data < 0.5 GB, against 39 GB free.

(8) Reuse: the LabSim code, seeds and eval hashes are released, so the whole dataset can be regenerated from code.
designs.compute_and_memory_plan:
MAC (M4 Pro, 48 GB; hard cap of 24 GB for everything we run together)

Before 11-06 (light only):
- writing code and running seconds-long numpy tests (< 1 GB)
- Commons API calls and model downloads (network only; defer any download that would take more than about 1 h)
- optional load probes of <= 10 min, one model at a time, under the memory guard

After 11-06, the product stack (estimates, to be measured on 11-09):
- mlx_vlm.server with Qwen3.5-9B MLX 4-bit: 5.98 GB
- adapter: about 0.09 GB
- KV cache and vision transients at 8k context and <= 1024 px: about 1-2 GB
- Streamlit, YOLOv8s and the referee: about 1-1.5 GB
- total: about 8-10 GB

The 27B on the Mac:
- Qwen3.8-27B MLX 4-bit takes about 18.5-21 GB with 8k context and one image.
- It runs only for baseline or parity checks, with the product stopped.
- Two LLMs are never loaded together: 9B + 27B would be about 27-29 GB.
- Images are downscaled to <= 1024 px and thinking is off.
- The memory guard stops the simplest task first above 22.5 GB.

Speed (estimates):
- 9B decode about 35-45 tok/s (bandwidth-based estimate), vs about 14 tok/s measured for the 27B architecture.
- That gives about 10 s per diagnosis for the 9B vs about 30 s for the 27B.

Disk: 27B 16.1 GB + 9B 6.0 GB + adapters + optional fallback GGUF 6.6 GB = <= 29 GB of the 39 GB free.

RTX 5090 (32 GB; from 11-06; jobs strictly one at a time)

Environment: CUDA >= 12.8 PyTorch for sm_120, transformers >= 5.2, flash-linear-attention and causal-conv1d, pinned in a lockfile. The first-run Gated DeltaNet kernel compile is budgeted.

Jobs and estimated wall-clock:
- data generation and freezing the eval sets: minutes
- untuned-9B eval with vLLM: 0.5-1 h
- SFT, bf16 LoRA at about 22 GB: <= 4 h box
- adapted eval: 0.5-1 h
- 27B baseline via llama.cpp Q4_K_M with parallel slots (16.8 + 0.93 GB + KV): 1.5-2.5 h
- shuffled-label control: 3-4 h, overnight
- RFT sampling + training: 1.5-2.5 h
- 4B run: 1-2 h
- optional cross-validation folds: 3-4 h each
- total: about 20-35 GPU-hours over 11-06 to 11-11 (estimate)

Throughput is measured in the first 10 minutes of each job, and the episode count is adjusted to fit the time box.

TRANSFER
- Mac -> server: only code, via git.
- Server -> Mac: adapters (about 87 MB), result logs and the GGUF fallback (about 6 GB), via a private Hugging Face repo or direct download.
- API baselines run from the Mac after 11-06 as light HTTP calls and are cached for the offline booth.
