designs.isef_compliance:
CATEGORY
ROBO > Machine Learning (alternative: Cognitive Systems). Framed as engineering criteria plus hypotheses with quantitative tests and statistics, so it is not a demonstration or explanation model.

CONTINUATION
- Declare it on Form 7, with the previous abstract and plan.
- The new line of investigation is the simulator-taught model, closed-loop diagnosis and measurement design. That is a substantive expansion.
- The board and abstract show only the new work.
- The earlier five classroom sessions and the 24/25-photo result are not presented.
- Ask the SRC whether the 809-image set and the June-Oct work count as prior research. If they do, E5b drops that set.

FORMS BEFORE EXPERIMENTATION
- Signed before any data generation, training or evaluation: the research plan (written by the student), Forms 1, 1A, 1B (with a parent) and Form 3 (risk assessment for his lab sessions: falling masses, moving carts).
- Tool development before that point is declared as development. The start date is the first data generation.
- Stay within 12 continuous months.
- List every phase now, because nothing can be added after the affiliated fair. Engineering iterations go in a Project Addendum.

HUMAN PARTICIPANTS
- The core experiments E1-E8 involve none and are exempt: simulator data, licensed public images, his own apparatus photos and measurements, and he is the only tester and rater.
- Check every image for identifiable people: crop, blur, or keep it off the board without releases.
- The 11-07 classroom use is normal teaching in classroom mode (referee results and checked templates only). No data are collected and nothing is reported.
- Any classroom or teacher study is a separate later phase. It needs:
  - a 3-member IRB (an educator who is not the sponsor, an administrator, a medical or mental-health professional) to sign Form 4 first
  - minor assent, plus parental permission with any survey attached
  - adult consent
  - de-identification by an adult
  - a written IRB/SRC ruling on showing AI feedback, given the Companion Guide's advice
- Teacher ratings of outputs would be human-participant data, so they are not used.

GENERATIVE AI (Rule 8, Form 2A)
- This design and all coding sessions are logged.
- AI-written code is listed per module and function in docs/AI_USAGE.md. Commit messages describe changes without naming tools, per the owner's repository rule.
- The AI-drafted LabSim cause and fix texts are disclosed and verified by him.
- AI does not write the plan, the abstract, the poster or paper drafts, the conclusions or the future work, and it supplies no citations. He reads and verifies every source himself; the names in this design come from verified research notes but still need his own reading.
- Grammar polishing is allowed only on his finished text, and is logged.

BOOTH
- Fully offline local model; API baselines precomputed; frozen build.
- No QR codes or URLs; generic model descriptions in the abstract.
- Every chart credited; licences respected (Apache-2.0 models, CC BY/BY-SA attribution).

INDEPENDENCE
He must be able to explain every module in the interview (25 points) and keep a dated lab notebook.
risks: The Qwen3.5 training stack on Blackwell (sm_120) fails or is slow: DeltaNet kernels, flash-linear-attention or causal-conv1d. Mitigation: a pinned CUDA >= 12.8 image; first-run compile time budgeted; fallback chain Unsloth -> ms-swift -> plain PEFT/TRL; Qwen3.5-4B as a fallback model; every job time-boxed.

The adapter conversion is silently wrong, so outputs equal the base model. Mitigation: a converter unit test before 11-06, the adapter-effect positive control and the 300-item parity test. Fallback: merge on the server -> GGUF Q4_K_M -> private HF repo -> LM Studio.

No transfer to held-out families (H1 fails). Mitigation: (1) it is pre-registered, so a miss is still a reportable result; (2) the ladder shows where the gain stops (L1/L2 vs L3); (3) the in-context and shuffled-label controls explain why; (4) the product still serves the six experiments exactly through the referee; (5) family cross-validation can follow after 11-15.

Shortcut learning on the synthetic data: rounding patterns, magnitude ranges, template strings, ID positions. Mitigation: randomized IDs and order, three paraphrases per text slot, overlapping magnitude priors, the L1-shift noise set, a classical-ML probe, and a leakage checker with a planted duplicate.

Simulator-to-real gap, and possibly no lab access for E8 before 11-15. Mitigation: literature-calibrated noise, shift tests and a prior-sensitivity analysis. Claims stay 'simulator-verified' until E8 data exist; E8 continues after 11-15 under the signed protocol.

Physics errors in the templates get baked into training. Mitigation: GPT's independent review, plus the student checking the curriculum families before SFT and all families before RFT. Any correction is recorded in a Project Addendum and the adapter is retrained.

The fine-tune degrades vision or general ability. Mitigation: the vision tower is frozen and E5 measures the effect. If a drop exceeds the margins, add 10-20% replay of the base model's own general answers (P1) and report the drop. Thinking-mode ability is not used and is not claimed to be preserved.
Breaching the 24 GB memory cap on the Mac. Mitigation: one LLM loaded at a time, images <= 1024 px, 8k context, and the guard stops the simplest task first above 22.5 GB.

Schedule slips: signatures not ready on 11-06, the GPU unavailable, or unknown server-to-Mac download speed. Mitigation: the variant schedule, a Hugging Face relay for adapters, and P0-only scope for 11-09.

ISEF integrity problems: forms dated after experimentation, overstated student work, AI drafting. Mitigation: forms first, the ledger and prompt logs, a student-written plan and conclusions, the interview drill, and SRC questions asked in writing.

The referee is misspecified: a wrong noise model makes the 'ground truth' wrong on real data. Mitigation: compare E8 results against the intended conditions, run a sensitivity analysis over noise priors, and report disagreements.

Local-server quirks: thinking not disabled, or broken JSON. Mitigation: mlx_vlm.server has thinking off by default, decoding is schema-constrained, and an automatic check confirms replies contain no reasoning block.

API baselines drift or fail on the schema. Mitigation: fixed subsets; logged model versions and dates; the same schema through each provider's structured-output feature; failures counted as failures; results cached for the offline booth.
Image provenance: the 809-image set includes frames of three online videos. Mitigation: use them for evaluation only and never display them. E5 can rest on the CC-licensed public set alone.
designs.why_it_wins:
IT MEETS THE TEACHER'S DEMAND
There is a real model upgrade, and its training signal is physics itself. A fault-injecting simulator and an exact Bayesian referee replace human labels and API teachers. The data are therefore unlimited, verifiable, and generated on the GPU without uploads.

IT ANSWERS THE STUDENT'S OPEN-SET WISH SCIENTIFICALLY
Instead of claiming the system 'recognizes anything', it measures whether a diagnostic skill learned on 18 experiments transfers to 6 it never saw. The six curriculum experiments stay exact and manually selectable.

IT TARGETS A DOCUMENTED WEAKNESS, NOT A RE-RUN
- Language models struggle with experimental design (BoxingGym) and with judging controlled experiments (Bewersdorff), and lab assistants give harmful or wrong replies.
- The current YOLO + chatbot design was already done by PhysicsAssistant.
- It differs from Sim2Reason, which uses simulator rewards for problem solving: here the model works on noisy measurements and chooses the next measurement.

THE EVALUATION IS ISEF-GRADE (Design 15, Execution 20)
- Acceptance lines are written before any run.
- Baselines are levelled on prompt, tool, schema and budget.
- Positive and negative controls, paired statistics with CIs, and an explicit list of what the upgrade must not change.
- So every outcome, including a null result, is informative.

THE ENGINEERING IS CREDIBLE AND VISIBLE (Creativity and Impact 20)
A 9B specialist goes head-to-head with the 27B generalist on the same laptop, fully offline and inside a 24 GB cap, with a 4B tier for school laptops.

IT PLAYS TO THE STUDENT'S PHYSICS
- Each error mechanism is physics he can defend in the 25-point interview: uncompensated friction, the (m+m_e)/M approximation, reaction-time bias, omitted rotational energy.
- The 'beat the detective' booth game makes the closed loop tangible to judges.

designs.name: CounterLab: counterfactual-tuned, conformal open-set recognition of school physics experiments on a laptop
designs.one_line_pitch: Photograph any lab setup and an offline 4B-parameter vision-language model returns the smallest set of experiments that is guaranteed to contain the right one 90% of the time. The model was re-trained on 'minimal pairs' made by digitally removing and adding apparatus in the student's existing 809 photos. It names the apparatus that decided its answer, and says 'not an experiment I know' or 'not a complete setup' instead of guessing. When a photo genuinely cannot tell (the cart+track case) it asks one question, and manual selection of the six curriculum experiments is always one click away.
designs.research_question: Does fine-tuning a small on-device vision-language model on apparatus-level counterfactual minimal pairs, built from existing lab photos, make its open-set recognition of school physics experiments causally grounded (its answer changes exactly when decisive apparatus changes) and conformally calibrated, compared with untuned local and frontier models?
hypotheses_or_criteria: H1 (baseline diagnosis): untuned VLMs (Qwen3.5-4B/9B, local Qwen3.8-27B, two frontier API models) have three predicted failures. (a) Their minimal-pair accuracy is significantly lower than the box-oracle positive control. (b) After subtracting matched-artifact controls, their answers change less often than the oracle's when decisive apparatus is deleted. (c) On photos the student marked visually undecidable, they give wrong single answers more often than alpha = 0.10. Tests: exact McNemar and one-sided exact binomial, Holm-corrected.

H2 (primary endpoint, the model upgrade): counterfactual evidence tuning (CET) of Qwen3.5-4B raises minimal-pair accuracy on held-out source groups by >= 10 percentage points over a data-matched SFT control (same base images and steps, no counterfactual pairs; exact McNemar). Clean-photo accuracy must be non-inferior: the one-sided 95% CI lower bound stays above -3 pp.

H3 (the guarantee and its limit): split-conformal sets calibrated on held-out in-domain groups cover the intended experiment at 90% +/- 3 pp (median of 1,000 random group-level splits, with a distribution consistent with the theoretical Beta law) and give wrong single answers <= 5% of the time. On external known-class photos the untuned model loses >= 10 pp of coverage, CET loses >= 5 pp less, and recalibrating with 30 target photos restores coverage to >= 88%.

H4 (open set): option-dropout CET improves AUROC by >= 0.05 over zero-shot maximum-probability scoring for experiment types never seen in training, while the conformal false-novelty rate on curriculum experiments stays <= 5%. Adding a held-out experiment's one-paragraph description to the registry, with no retraining, gives >= 70% top-1 on its photos; removing the description sends >= 80% of them to 'not listed'.

H5 (small tuned vs big untuned): CET-4B is non-inferior to untuned Qwen3.8-27B in minimal-pair accuracy (margin 3 pp) and mean conformal set size (margin 0.1 options), while using <= 1/4 of its memory and <= 1/3 of its latency on the M4 Pro.

H6 (simulated closed loop, P1): showing the conformal set plus one expected-information-gain question cuts a simulated user's wrong-experiment-form rate by >= 50% compared with accepting the top-1 suggestion, with <= 1.3 questions per photo on average.

Engineering criteria (pass/fail, pre-registered): the product runs fully offline with no API; recognizer p95 latency <= 8 s per 768 px photo on the M4 Pro; whole-app peak memory <= 12 GB and never above the 24 GB cap; Mac 4-bit vs server bf16 top-1 agreement >= 95% with coverage change <= 2 pp; manual selection reachable in <= 2 clicks at every step.
All numeric thresholds above are suggestions. The student fixes the final values himself in his own research plan before the first data-generating run (planned 11-07).
designs.product_experience:
STUDENT (offline laptop, Streamlit):
1) Upload a photo of the setup (or a clip of 10 s or less, P2).
2) Tab 1, unchanged: YOLOv8s draws boxes for the six apparatus classes and the student fixes them on the canvas.
3) Tab 2, 'Which experiment?': the tuned on-device model returns a conformal prediction set shown as chips, with the line 'the right experiment is in this set 9 times out of 10 (calibrated on photos like yours)'.
- One chip: 'Recognised: friction', with the deciding apparatus outlined (for example, the spring scale pulling the block).
- Several chips, such as the cart+track tie between average speed, Newton's 2nd law and energy: the app asks the single question that best splits the set ('What will you measure? time over a marked distance / acceleration with a hanging weight / speed at the bottom of the slope'). One tap resolves it.
- 'Not a complete experiment': 'I can only see a track; include the cart and the measuring tool, or pick the experiment yourself.' No forced guess.
- 'Not in your course list': an unknown-experiment panel offers the closest teacher-registered extra (for example, pendulum). Otherwise it shows a draft card (P2: name, variables, candidate law, and a generic two-column data table with law fitting) marked 'draft - check with your teacher'.
- A dropdown with the six curriculum experiments, the registered extras and 'Other' is always visible. Choosing manually overrides everything and is logged locally.
4) The experiment form, readings, physics.py result and animation work as today. The explanation is a deterministic template filled with physics.py numbers (optionally rephrased by the local model, with a number checker), so no unchecked AI text is shown by default. The GLM API is removed.

TEACHER:
1) Registry page: shows the six experiment signatures (necessary apparatus, configuration, what is measured, governing law). The teacher can add an experiment by writing a one-paragraph description plus its variables and law. It becomes an option at once, with no retraining (tested in E4).
2) Recalibration page: for a new kit or classroom, the teacher labels about 30 photos to re-establish the 90% guarantee (tested in E3).
3) Local session summary: counts of recognised, ambiguous and incomplete setups and of manual overrides, with no names and no images of people.

During the ISEF research phase only the student researcher operates the app. Teachers and classmates use it only as ordinary teaching, or under an IRB-approved protocol (E8).

technical_components.name: Experiment signature table + identifiability calculus
technical_components.what: A machine-readable registry of the six curriculum experiments plus a 15-type library of other school experiments (simple pendulum, free fall with ticker tape, Atwood machine, horizontal projectile, mass-spring oscillation, lever balance, buoyancy, liquid pressure, inclined-plane friction coefficient, lens focal length, refraction block, Ohm's law, specific heat, electroscope/Van de Graaff). Each entry records: (1) necessary apparatus roles mapped to the six detector classes (cart, track, string, dynamometer, wooden_block, iron_block); (2) configuration cues outside that vocabulary (pulley + hanging mass, incline, speed gate/ticker timer, stopwatch with start/finish marks, vertical spring with masses); (3) what is measured; (4) the governing law; (5) a one-paragraph description used as option text. Functions: admissible_set(visible apparatus) returns the experiments consistent with the evidence; edit_label(edit, image) returns the new target after a deletion or addition; a theoretical non-identifiability matrix records, for example, that a single cart + track admits average speed, Newton's 2nd law and energy conservation (the proven tie). The library is split into 'training distractor' types and held-out types reserved for the open-set and registry-extension tests. The student checks and signs off the physics content.
technical_components.novelty_vs_prior_art: Formalises 'what you measure, not what you see, defines the experiment' and turns the cart+track tie into set-valued ground truth. Conformal prediction under ambiguous ground truth exists (Stutz et al., TMLR 2023; Caprio & Stutz 2024), but there the ambiguity comes from annotators disagreeing; here it is derived from the measurement structure of each experiment. No such registry turned up in the verified prior-art search.
technical_components.feasibility_and_memory: Pure Python/YAML, kilobytes of RAM, no model. The coding assistant drafts it (recorded in the ledger); the student approves the content.

technical_components.name: Counterfactual Lab-Setup Benchmark (CLSB) generator + natural minimal-pair miner
technical_components.what: A seeded generator that works from the human-verified YOLO boxes of the 809 images. Edit types: (1) critical deletions of necessary-role objects, by box occlusion with local mean colour or by classical Telea inpainting on a dilated mask; (2) matched-artifact controls: the same mask and fill placed on background that touches no apparatus box; (3) additions: a donor cart or block from the same split pasted at track scale with feathered edges; (4) label-preserving nuisance transforms: crop to the apparatus union, 512/768/1024 px, JPEG q35, brightness/contrast, grayscale, horizontal flip, background blur outside boxes. Every variant carries a pair id, edit type, programmatic target and the split of its base image. A miner finds natural (unedited) minimal pairs in existing sessions and videos: same session by EXIF time, similar background by pHash/SSIM outside the boxes, apparatus multisets differing by one element. The student verifies them.
technical_components.novelty_vs_prior_art: Minimal-pair VLM benchmarks (Winoground, MMVP, NaturalBench), occlusion analysis (Zeiler & Fergus) and object masking for counterfactual training (CSS, CVPR 2020) already exist. Not found: apparatus-level minimal pairs with physics-derived label changes, matched-artifact controls and mined natural pairs, used to test whether a model identifies the experiment.
technical_components.feasibility_and_memory: OpenCV + numpy on the Mac CPU, under 1 GB RAM, minutes for an estimated 5-8k variants (0.5-1 GB disk). The server produces identical output from the same seed, confirmed by a 20-image checksum test. Runs are scheduled before, never during, 27B runs.

technical_components.name: Equalised option-scoring harness
technical_components.what: One prompt and one scoring rule for every arm. The options are lettered: registry descriptions plus 'not listed' plus 'not a complete experiment'. Thinking is off, and images are resized to 768 px on the long side. Each option's probability is the renormalised log-probability of its letter token at the first answer position (mlx_vlm.server top_logprobs on the Mac; transformers on the server). Option-order bias is measured with a reversed order on a subset. API models are scored by answer frequency over 5 samples (logit-free conformal) plus their stated answer. Every prompt and response is logged with hashes (needed for Form 2A).
technical_components.novelty_vs_prior_art: None claimed. This is the baseline equalisation (same prompt, options, resolution, scorer and budget) that makes the comparisons fair.
technical_components.feasibility_and_memory: Memory is only the loaded model. Estimates on the M4 Pro: 27B about 9 s per image at 768 px (430-580 visual + ~350 text tokens at the measured ~115 tok/s prefill, one decoded token); 4B about 2-3 s.

technical_components.name: Counterfactual evidence tuning (CET-LoRA) of Qwen3.5-4B - the model-level upgrade
technical_components.what: LoRA (r=16, alpha=32) on the language-model linear layers whose names map one-to-one to the MLX implementation; vision tower frozen. The loss has four terms: (1) soft-label cross-entropy on the answer-letter token; (2) symmetric KL consistency between each image and its nuisance variants; (3) a hinge margin requiring log p(original experiment) to fall more on a critical deletion than on its matched-artifact control, so 'edit artifact means change' cannot be learned; (4) a short evidence-list target naming the necessary-role apparatus. Option dropout: each example shows a random subset and order of 4-8 options from the registry and the training-distractor types, and when the true experiment is withheld the target is 'not listed'. Targets are one-hot for decidable photos, uniform over the admissible set for photos marked undecidable, and 'not a complete experiment' for parts-only photos and decisive deletions. Ablation ladder: data-matched SFT, augmentation only, full CET, full CET without option dropout.
technical_components.novelty_vs_prior_art: Counterfactual augmentation and consistency losses for VLMs exist: CSS (CVPR 2020), CF-VLM (NeurIPS 2025, arXiv 2506.17267), and an edit-consistency SFT paper (arXiv 2506.07227) that the student must read. The new combination is: physics-derived counterfactual and set-valued targets, matched-artifact negatives against edit shortcuts, and option dropout that creates open-set training signal from closed-set photos, all trained for conformal use on-device in a lab-teaching domain. No frontier-API or teacher-model outputs are used.
technical_components.feasibility_and_memory: RTX 5090 (32 GB). bf16 LoRA needs about 10 GB VRAM for 4B and about 22 GB for 9B (Unsloth table). Estimated 3-5k examples at 768 px and 0.5-1.5 h per 4B run, 7-8 runs in total. The adapter is about 65 MB (4B) or 87 MB (9B). It deploys on the 3.06 GB 4-bit MLX base.

technical_components.name: Conformal open-set layer
technical_components.what: (1) Split conformal over the full option space with LAC and APS scores. (2) Mondrian (class-conditional) calibration for classes with at least 20 calibration units. (3) Conformal novelty p-values, ranking the 'not listed' statistic among in-distribution calibration scores, which route a photo to the unknown-experiment path with a guaranteed false-novelty rate alpha_n on curriculum experiments. (4) Group-aware calibration: whole videos or sessions go to calibration or to test, and frames are sub-sampled per video segment. (5) Diagnostics: coverage over 1,000 random group splits compared with the theoretical Beta(n+1-l, l) distribution. (6) Target-domain recalibration with m labelled photos, which is also the teacher recalibration page. (7) Monte-Carlo conformal for undecidable photos as a secondary analysis. The same layer wraps the existing rule classifier as a 'conformalised rules' baseline.
technical_components.novelty_vs_prior_art: Conformal sets already exist for zero-shot VLM classification (Silva-Rodriguez et al., CVPR 2025), LLM multiple-choice QA (Kumar et al. 2023) and logit-free APIs (Su et al. 2024). The verified search found none for experiment-type recognition, and none combined with physics-derived ambiguity and novelty routing.
technical_components.feasibility_and_memory: numpy, milliseconds per photo, no extra model. Unit-tested on simulated scores before any real data is touched.

technical_components.name: On-device serving, adapter converter and memory watchdog
technical_components.what: (1) A PEFT-to-MLX adapter converter (key renaming, lora_A/B transposes, scale = alpha/r) with a round-trip unit test on tiny random tensors. (2) mlx_vlm.server serving the 4-bit MLX base plus adapter (--adapter-path, top_logprobs, thinking off, --max-pixels cap). It reuses the model folders downloaded by lms, so there are no duplicate 16 GB copies and no fusing; LM Studio itself cannot load adapters. (3) A watchdog that samples the total footprint of our processes every 2 s and, above 24 GB, stops the cheapest-to-restart process first. (4) An MLX memory limit on each server process. Bionic is quit during 27B runs.
technical_components.novelty_vs_prior_art: Engineering only; no novelty claimed.
technical_components.feasibility_and_memory: Estimates: recognizer process 5 GB or less with the 4B; whole app 7-8 GB. The 27B (est. 18.5-21 GB) is only ever loaded alone, for baseline runs.

technical_components.name: Product UI with manual selection preserved
technical_components.what: Streamlit tab 2 is rebuilt around the prediction set: chips with a one-line guarantee; an outline of the deciding apparatus; a one-tap clarifying question; 'not a complete experiment' and 'not in your course list' panels; and an always-visible manual dropdown (six curriculum experiments, registered extras, Other) that overrides everything and is logged locally. Adds a teacher registry page (add an experiment by description) and a recalibration page. physics.py forms, results and animations are unchanged. The default explanation is a deterministic template; the GLM API is removed.
technical_components.novelty_vs_prior_art: Product framing: manual selection is kept but becomes faster and honest about uncertainty. No novelty claimed for the UI code.
technical_components.feasibility_and_memory: Streamlit plus existing modules; negligible memory.

technical_components.name: Pre-registration, controls and statistics package
technical_components.what: Before any test run, the dated lab notebook records the SHA-256 of the test lists, the signature table, the prompts and the hyperparameters. Controls: positive control (rules on ground-truth boxes), negative control (blank image), matched-artifact controls. Statistics: exact McNemar; cluster bootstrap 95% CIs over source groups; Wilson and Clopper-Pearson intervals; Holm correction across four primary endpoints; one-sided non-inferiority tests; AUROC with paired bootstrap; ECE with reliability diagrams; risk-coverage curves; scripted figures. Every analysis is run by the student.
technical_components.novelty_vs_prior_art: Methodological rigour that ISEF scores under Design and Execution. It follows the approach of the Gewu reference paper the student admired: dated acceptance lines, equalised baselines, positive controls.
technical_components.feasibility_and_memory: numpy/scipy/matplotlib; negligible memory.

technical_components.name: Expected-information-gain clarifying question + simulated closed loop
technical_components.what: A bank of about 10 questions whose answer likelihoods come from the signature table (for example 'hanging weight over a pulley?', 'what will you measure?'). The question with the highest mutual information with the experiment label, given the current set, is asked. A simulated user answers from ground truth with 0, 5 or 10% answer noise. Compared against top-1 acceptance and dropdown-only.
technical_components.novelty_vs_prior_art: Choosing the next query to minimise entropy goes back to GDE (de Kleer & Williams 1987); CLAM asks clarifying questions only when needed. BoxingGym shows LLMs struggle with EIG-style choices, so here EIG is computed explicitly from the registry rather than by the LLM, and is used to resolve an experiment-identity set.
technical_components.feasibility_and_memory: Trivial compute, no humans.

technical_components.name: External open-set test suite with licence manifest
technical_components.what: Four pools: (1) Wikimedia Commons stills; (2) keyframes from the Getaclass CC BY 3.0 video lessons and the Macedonian Wikiexperiments CC BY-SA 4.0 videos; (3) PhysiSens CC BY 4.0 single-instrument images as 'not an experiment'; (4) optional Physics-IQ CC BY clips, evaluation only. They are grouped into known-class out-of-distribution photos, held-out unknown types (test only), training-distractor types (CC BY/CC0/PD images only) and non-experiments. Inclusion criteria are fixed before any model output is seen: real apparatus, setup visible, no identifiable people, licence OK. A per-file attribution manifest records title, author, URL and licence.
technical_components.novelty_vs_prior_art: Not found in prior art: a known-unknown versus unknown-unknown protocol in the Scheirer / Vaze open-set tradition applied to physics-lab setups.
technical_components.feasibility_and_memory: Commons thumbnails (960/1280 px, under 1 GB) are fetched within the API limits (200 requests/min, at most 2 parallel downloads). Video transcodes and PhysiSens (201 MB) are fetched on the server, and only small keyframe or sample sets move to the Mac.

technical_components.name: Evidence citation and deletion-faithfulness test
technical_components.what: The tuned model names the apparatus that decided its answer. The test deletes all ground-truth boxes of the cited classes, and separately an equal-area set of non-cited boxes or background. Faithfulness = change rate when cited evidence is deleted minus change rate when non-cited evidence is deleted. The product outlines the cited boxes.
technical_components.novelty_vs_prior_art: Deletion-based faithfulness checks exist in explainable AI generally (the student should find and read the sources). Here they are applied at object level with physics roles.
technical_components.feasibility_and_memory: Reuses CLSB tooling; one extra scoring pass on the server.

technical_components.name: Scale and input ablations
technical_components.what: CET on Qwen3.5-9B. Input variants: Set-of-Mark overlay (numbered YOLO boxes drawn on the image) vs raw image vs raw image plus the apparatus list as text. Resolutions 512/768/1024 px. Option-order permutation test. A thinking-on prompting arm for the 27B on a subset of 100-200 items.
technical_components.novelty_vs_prior_art: Standard ablations; they answer the judge's question 'why train instead of prompting or using a bigger model?'.
technical_components.feasibility_and_memory: 9B LoRA about 22 GB VRAM on the 5090. On the Mac the 9B 4-bit base is 5.98 GB, giving an estimated 10-11 GB app. The thinking-on 27B arm is slow at about 14 tok/s decode, so it is limited to a subset.

technical_components.name: Open-world experiment card + generic law fitting
technical_components.what: For 'not listed' photos, the local model fills a constrained-JSON card: name, apparatus, independent, dependent and controlled variables, and a candidate law chosen from a fixed library (linear, proportional, inverse, square, square-root, power law). A numpy fitter picks the functional form by BIC from data the student enters and reports the constants with uncertainty. Shown only as a labelled draft, and never to research participants.
technical_components.novelty_vs_prior_art: LLM law-discovery benchmarks (LLM-SR, NewtonBench, PhysGym) do far more. This is a small fixed library aimed at school data, and it is the product's answer to 'any experiment'.
technical_components.feasibility_and_memory: numpy fitter. If the 27B writes the card, the 4B is unloaded first, so only one VLM is in memory.

technical_components.name: Qwen3.8-27B QLoRA CET (server only)
technical_components.what: Repeat full CET on the 27B with Unsloth QLoRA to test whether scale and CET compound. Evaluation stays on the server only.
technical_components.novelty_vs_prior_art: Same method as above, at a larger scale.
technical_components.feasibility_and_memory: Unsloth's Qwen3.8 guide says QLoRA fits in 24 GB, but its Qwen3.5 guide advises against QLoRA for this family, and bnb-4bit vs MLX affine 4-bit is a mismatch. Adapter is 160-235 MB. Only if the P0/P1 runs finish early.

technical_components.name: Video (multi-frame) recognition
technical_components.what: Send 4-8 keyframes from a clip as one multi-image query, and test whether motion shrinks conformal sets on ambiguous scenes, using the existing clips and the CC video lessons.
technical_components.novelty_vs_prior_art: Exploratory. The existing in-domain video covers only friction and steel-ball setups.
technical_components.feasibility_and_memory: Several images multiply visual tokens; frames are capped at 512 px and the 4B is used.

technical_components.name: Hidden-state probe of the frozen VLM
technical_components.what: Linear probes on image-token states test whether the untuned model internally encodes the decisive apparatus (for example, number of carts) on CLSB pairs even when its answer ignores it.
technical_components.novelty_vs_prior_art: Builds on 'Hidden in plain sight' (Fu et al. 2025) and first-token probing (Zhao et al., ECCV 2024), applied here to lab-apparatus evidence.
technical_components.feasibility_and_memory: Activation extraction with mlx-vlm hooks: the 27B alone (est. 19-21 GB) after 11-09, or the 4B/9B on the server.

designs.model_upgrade:
WHAT IS TRAINED
- LoRA adapters (r=16, alpha=32, dropout 0.05) on the language-model linear layers of the official Qwen3.5-4B vision-language model: attention and MLP projections whose names map one-to-one to the MLX implementation. The vision tower is frozen.
- Qwen3.5-9B is a secondary arm. A Qwen3.8-27B QLoRA run is P2 and server-only.
- Method: counterfactual evidence tuning (CET). The loss has four terms:
  (a) Soft-label cross-entropy on a single answer-letter token over the presented options. Targets are one-hot for decidable photos, uniform over the physics-admissible set for photos the student marks undecidable, and 'not a complete experiment' for parts-only photos and decisive-evidence deletions.
  (b) Symmetric KL consistency between an image and its label-preserving variants.
  (c) A hinge margin that makes log p(original experiment) fall more on a label-changing deletion than on its matched-artifact control, so the model cannot learn 'edit artifact means change'.
  (d) A short evidence-list target naming the necessary-role apparatus.
- Option dropout: each example presents a random subset and order of 4-8 options from the registry and the training-distractor library. When the true experiment is withheld the target is 'not listed', which gives open-set training signal from closed-set photos and teaches matching evidence to descriptions.

DATA SOURCE
- Generated by seeded code on the GPU server from the training groups of the 809 annotated images. The server pulls dataset.zip from the public GitHub repo, so nothing has to be uploaded.
- Labels come from the signature table plus the student's intended-experiment and decidability labels (a CSV of a few KB is uploaded).
- Optionally, 100-200 CC BY/CC0 images of training-distractor types; held-out types never enter training.
- No frontier-API or teacher-model outputs are used for training.

COMPUTE LOCATION
- Rented RTX 5090 (32 GB), PyTorch with PEFT (ms-swift recipe, or a transformers custom Trainer; Unsloth as fallback). Needs a CUDA 12.8+ torch build for sm_120 and transformers >= 5.2.
- bf16 LoRA uses about 10 GB VRAM for the 4B and about 22 GB for the 9B (Unsloth table). Images are capped at 768 px.
- Estimate: 0.5-1.5 h per 4B run, 7-8 runs: data-matched SFT control x2 seeds, CET full x2 seeds, augmentation-only, no-option-dropout, CET-9B.
- Hyperparameters, prompts and SHA-256 test lists are frozen in the dated plan before any test evaluation. Early stopping uses a validation group only.

DEPLOYMENT PATH
- The adapter (~65 MB for 4B, ~87 MB for 9B) is downloaded to the Mac.
- A small tested script converts it from PEFT to MLX (key renaming, A/B transposes, scale = alpha/r).
- It is served on the 4-bit MLX base (3.06 GB / 5.98 GB) with mlx_vlm.server --adapter-path. LM Studio cannot load adapters, and no fused 16 GB copies are made.
- The product's recognizer runs in about 5 GB; the whole app in about 7-8 GB (estimate).

HOW IT IS MEASURED
- Primary: minimal-pair accuracy on held-out source groups, CET full vs the data-matched SFT control (same images and steps, no counterfactuals, no option dropout), exact McNemar, Holm-corrected.
- Secondary:
  - clean-photo non-inferiority (margin 3 pp)
  - excess counterfactual sensitivity over matched controls, and nuisance invariance
  - inadmissible-error rate
  - conformal coverage, set size and wrong-singleton rate in-domain and under shift
  - open-set AUROC and registry-extension accuracy
  - ECE
  - evidence faithfulness
  - non-inferiority vs untuned 27B
  - Mac latency and peak memory
  - Mac 4-bit vs server bf16 agreement (deployment fidelity)
- References: the untuned 4B/9B/27B and two frontier API models, all with identical prompts, options, resolution and scoring.

experiments.name: E1 Shortcut diagnosis of untuned models on the counterfactual benchmark
experiments.data: CLSB-test built only from held-out test groups: an estimated 150-250 deduplicated clean base images, about 1,000 edited variants (critical deletions, matched-artifact controls, additions, nuisance transforms), and the student-marked decidable/undecidable single-cart + track photos.
experiments.arms_and_baselines: Positive control: rules on ground-truth boxes. Current system: rules on YOLO-predicted boxes (optimistic, because the existing YOLO split was not group-aware and the detector saw frames from every video), plus the same rules with conformal calibration. Untuned Qwen3.5-4B, Qwen3.5-9B and local Qwen3.8-27B (4-bit MLX, thinking off). The 27B with thinking on and full signature descriptions on a 100-200 item subset, as the strongest prompting arm. Two frontier API VLMs, precomputed with 5-sample answer frequencies. Negative control: a blank image with the same options. All arms use the identical prompt, options, 768 px image-only input and scorer.
experiments.metrics_and_stats: Primary per model: minimal-pair accuracy. A pair counts as correct only if top-1 is admissible for both images and, for a label-changing edit, the invalidated experiment is no longer top-1. Secondary: excess sensitivity (change rate on critical edits minus change rate on matched-artifact controls); invariance under nuisance edits; inadmissible-error rate (top-1 outside the admissible set); share of errors falling inside theoretically non-identifiable pairs; wrong-singleton rate on undecidable photos vs alpha = 0.10 (one-sided exact binomial). Tests: exact McNemar for critical vs matched control, paired by base image; cluster bootstrap 95% CIs over source groups; Holm correction across models.
experiments.sample_size: About 1,000 pairs (at least 150 per edit type) from an estimated 150-250 base images. Power estimate: about 85 independent pairs detect a 15 pp paired difference at 25% discordance (alpha 0.05, power 0.8). With a design effect of 2-3 for correlated edits, 170-260 pairs are needed, so about 1,000 is ample.
experiments.human_participants_status: None. The student alone runs the system on his own apparatus photos (screened for people) and on public data. Exempt; no IRB needed.

experiments.name: E2 Counterfactual evidence tuning vs a data-matched control (primary endpoint, H2 and H5)
experiments.data: Training: CET data from the training groups only (an estimated 3-5k examples, including variants, parts-only 'not a complete experiment' photos and optional CC BY/CC0 distractor-type images). Testing: the E1 items plus clean test photos. One validation group is used for early stopping only.
experiments.arms_and_baselines: (a) untuned Qwen3.5-4B; (b) data-matched SFT: same base images and steps, no counterfactual pairs, no option dropout; (c) CET augmentation only, without the consistency and margin terms; (d) CET full; (e) CET full without option dropout; (f) CET-9B (P1). References: untuned 27B and the API arms from E1. Arms (b) and (d) are trained with 2 seeds each.
experiments.metrics_and_stats: Primary: minimal-pair accuracy of (d) vs (b), exact McNemar, Holm-corrected together with the E3/E4 primary endpoints. Clean admissible top-1 accuracy must be non-inferior (one-sided 95% CI lower bound above -3 pp). Secondary: excess sensitivity, invariance, inadmissible-error rate, ECE with reliability diagrams, set size at 90% coverage, evidence faithfulness (P1), seed-to-seed spread. H5: non-inferiority of (d) vs untuned 27B (margin 3 pp), with memory and latency ratios from E7.
experiments.sample_size: The same ~1,000 pairs and an estimated 150-250 clean test photos as E1; 7-8 training runs.
experiments.human_participants_status: None (exempt).

experiments.name: E3 Conformal coverage: in-domain guarantee, domain shift and recalibration (H3)
experiments.data: Calibration groups and test groups, both disjoint from training. An external known-class out-of-distribution set: Commons stills plus CC video-lesson keyframes of friction, Hooke's law, inclined plane, uniform motion, free fall, force and mass (an estimated 80-150 images). Hooke's law has no in-domain photos, so it is a described-but-unseen class.
experiments.arms_and_baselines: Score sources: conformalised rules, untuned 4B, untuned 27B, CET-4B. Score functions: LAC vs APS. Calibration: marginal vs Mondrian (classes with at least 20 calibration units). Out-of-distribution: no recalibration vs recalibration with m = 10, 20 or 30 target photos (200 random draws each). Monte-Carlo conformal for undecidable items as a secondary analysis.
experiments.metrics_and_stats: Empirical coverage of the intended experiment, mean set size, singleton rate, wrong-singleton rate and class-conditional coverage. The coverage distribution over 1,000 random group-level calibration/test splits is compared with the theoretical Beta(n+1-l, l) distribution. Clopper-Pearson CIs. Paired bootstrap for the difference in out-of-distribution coverage loss between untuned and CET. A recalibration curve (coverage vs m).
experiments.sample_size: In-domain: an estimated 100-200 calibration and 150-250 test units, with frames sub-sampled per video segment. Out-of-distribution: an estimated 80-150 images. The Wilson 95% CI half-width is about +/-4 pp at n = 200.
experiments.human_participants_status: None (exempt; public CC images with attribution).

experiments.name: E4 Open-set detection and registry extension (H4)
experiments.data: Held-out unknown types never used in training (for example, optical bench/lenses, refraction, pendulum, electroscopes/Van de Graaff; an estimated 100-150 images). Known-class images from E3. 100 single-instrument PhysiSens images as 'not an experiment'. Registry-extension subsets in which a held-out experiment's description is added at test time.
experiments.arms_and_baselines: Zero-shot maximum probability; zero-shot probability of the 'not listed' option; CET without option dropout; CET with option dropout. Each uses conformal novelty p-values at alpha_n = 0.05, calibrated on in-domain known classes. Registry extension is run with and without the new description.
experiments.metrics_and_stats: AUROC and FPR at 95% TPR for unknown vs known; false-novelty rate on known classes (guaranteed at most 0.05 in-domain, measured out-of-distribution); 'not a complete experiment' rate on single instruments; registry-extension top-1, and the 'not listed' rate when the description is absent. Bootstrap CIs, paired bootstrap for AUROC differences, Holm correction.
experiments.sample_size: An estimated 100-150 unknown, 150-250 known and 100 non-experiment images; at least 20 images per added experiment where available.
experiments.human_participants_status: None (exempt).

experiments.name: E5 Natural minimal pairs: do gains on synthetic edits transfer to real apparatus changes?
experiments.data: Unedited photo or frame pairs from the same session and viewpoint that differ by one apparatus element (for example, one vs two carts, or a block with and without the spring scale). They are mined automatically and verified by the student; an estimated 20-60 pairs.
experiments.arms_and_baselines: Rules on ground-truth boxes, untuned 4B, CET-4B, untuned 27B, API baselines.
experiments.metrics_and_stats: Natural minimal-pair accuracy with exact Clopper-Pearson CIs; exact McNemar for CET-4B vs untuned 4B; per-model agreement between synthetic-pair and natural-pair accuracy. Reported as exploratory if fewer than 40 pairs.
experiments.sample_size: An estimated 20-60 pairs. The count is fixed after mining and before any scoring.
experiments.human_participants_status: None.

experiments.name: E6 Simulated clarification loop: a closed loop without participants (H6, P1)
experiments.data: All in-domain and out-of-distribution test images with ground truth, plus the question bank of about 10 questions with answer likelihoods from the signature table.
experiments.arms_and_baselines: Top-1 acceptance (current behaviour); dropdown only; conformal set plus a fixed-order question; conformal set plus the expected-information-gain question. Simulated answer noise of 0, 5 and 10%.

designs.data_plan:
1) IN-DOMAIN DATA (all existing; no new photos)
- 809 YOLO-annotated images: 241 self-captured photos (IMG_9307-9572; 266 HEIC originals with EXIF are in the repo) and 568 frames from 6 clips of 3 source videos.
- Box combinations (counted from the label files):
  - friction setups (block + spring scale): about 330 frames, 2 source videos
  - steel ball + track: about 230 frames, 1 source video
  - single cart + track (with or without string): about 95 photos
  - two-cart scenes: about 23
  - parts-only shots (cart, track or string alone, or cart + string): about 115
  - Hooke's law: effectively absent in-domain
- The server and the Mac both fetch data/dataset.zip from the public repo.

2) NEW LABELS, BY THE STUDENT ONLY (after the forms are signed; about 3 h in a keyboard-driven gallery pre-filled by rules)
- Intended experiment per photo or clip, or 'not a complete experiment' for parts-only shots: about 45 min.
- For each single-cart + track photo, a 'visually decidable?' tick and the decisive cue (pulley + hanging mass / incline + speed gate / start-finish marks / none): about 25 min.
- Verification of mined natural pairs: about 10 min.
- A blind re-label of a random 20% one day later, for intra-rater kappa: about 15 min.
- Verification of external labels against the pre-registered inclusion criteria: about 60 min.

3) GROUPS AND SPLITS
- Groups are video sources (atomic) and photo sessions (EXIF time gap over 10 min, read with macOS sips/mdls).
- Group split 60/20/20 into train/calibration/test, stratified so that friction and cart experiments appear in every split. The single ball video is split by clip and flagged.
- Near-duplicates are removed across splits with a numpy pHash. Every edited variant inherits its base image's split.
- Test lists are SHA-256 hashed in the notebook before training.
- The old YOLO train/val/test split is not used for recognition because it is not group-aware.

4) COUNTERFACTUAL BENCHMARK (CLSB)
- Seeded code over ground-truth boxes: critical deletions (occlusion and Telea inpainting), matched-artifact controls, donor additions from the same split, nuisance transforms, and mined natural pairs (an estimated 20-60).
- An estimated 5-8k variants (0.5-1 GB), regenerated identically on the Mac and the server (checksum test).

5) EXTERNAL OPEN-SET DATA (public, cited, with a per-file attribution manifest)
- Sources:
  - Wikimedia Commons stills via the API with a contact User-Agent (at most 200 requests/min, at most 2 parallel downloads, 960/1280 px thumbnails). Categories such as Hooke's law, Spring scales, Inclined planes, Pendulums, Optical benches, Refraction, Electroscopes, Van de Graaff generators, Calorimeters, Breadboards and Physics experiments.
  - Keyframes, 3 per video at 25/50/75%, from the Getaclass CC BY 3.0 lessons and the Macedonian Wikiexperiments CC BY-SA 4.0 videos (480p transcodes, extracted on the server).
  - 100 single-instrument images sampled from PhysiSens (CC BY 4.0) as 'not an experiment'.
  - Optionally, Physics-IQ (CC BY) clips, evaluation only, per its rules.
- Inclusion criteria (real apparatus, setup visible, no identifiable people, licence OK) are written into the plan and applied before any model output is seen; every rejection reason is logged.
- Pools (estimates):
  - known-class out-of-distribution: 80-150
  - held-out unknown types, test only: 100-150
  - training-distractor types, CC BY/CC0/PD only: 100-200
  - non-experiments: 100
- CC BY-SA files are used for testing only. Only small subsets cross the slow upload link (a ~30-50 MB thumbnail subset takes about 5-8 min at 100 KB/s).

6) PRIVACY
- The COCO yolov8n.pt already in the Proj folder flags any image containing a person. The student blurs or excludes it.
- No faces on the poster or in demo screenshots.

7) EXCLUDED UNLESS THE SRC AGREES
- The 25-photo intent set and anything from the five earlier classroom sessions. With SRC agreement they could become a sealed real-use test set, never used for training.

8) PROVENANCE
- A data card records sources, licences, seeds, hashes and label protocols.
- An AI-usage ledger identifies AI-written data code.
designs.compute_and_memory_plan:
MAC (M4 Pro, 48 GB; hard cap 24 GB for everything we run together; about 39 GB free disk)
- Models:
  - Qwen3.5-4B MLX 4-bit (3.06 GB): recognizer in the product and in evaluation.
  - Qwen3.8-27B MLX 4-bit (16.08 GB): untuned local baseline; optional card writer, P2.
  - Qwen3.5-9B MLX 4-bit (5.98 GB): optional.
  - Never two VLMs loaded at once. mlx_vlm.server (installed in a venv with the user's approval) reads the folders downloaded by lms, so no duplicate copies are made. Bionic is quit during 27B runs.
- Product mode (estimate): 4B recognizer at most 5 GB + YOLOv8s 0.5-1 GB + Streamlit about 0.5 GB + browser about 1 GB = about 7-8 GB. The 9B variant is about 10-11 GB.
- 27B baseline mode:
  - Only the 27B loaded (about 18.5-21 GB estimated, at 8k context with one 768 px image). MLX memory limit about 21 GB; --max-pixels cap; no Streamlit, browser or YOLO.
  - The evaluation client checkpoints after every item, so it is the first thing stopped and resumed if total use passes 24 GB.
- Watchdog: samples the total footprint of our processes every 2 s. Kill order is cheapest-to-restart first: edit generator, then evaluation client, then model server.
- Throughput (estimate, from the measured ~115 tok/s prefill):
  - 27B: about 9 s per scored photo at 768 px (430-580 visual + ~350 text tokens, one decoded token), so about 1,600 items per overnight run of about 4 h.
  - 4B: about 2-3 s per item.
- Edit generation: OpenCV/numpy on the CPU, under 1 GB, run before (not during) 27B runs.
- Disk: 27B + 4B (+9B) = 19-25 GB; data, variants and external images at most 3 GB; adapters under 0.5 GB. No fused models and no bf16 bases on the Mac.
- Before 11-06 only: code, plus unit tests on synthetic toy data, plus one memory/logprob/thinking-off probe per model of 10 minutes or less on 3 synthetic images (outputs discarded; development testing, not data).

RTX 5090 (32 GB, rented from 11-06 for setup; data runs only from 11-07)
- Data flow:
  - Code arrives by git (a few KB). The dataset comes from the public GitHub repo. Base models come from Hugging Face, with ModelScope as fallback if the server's region blocks HF. CC video transcodes and PhysiSens are fetched directly.
  - Uploads from the Mac are limited to a few MB (for example, the student's label CSV).
  - Downloads to the Mac: adapters (about 65-87 MB each) and result tables (MB). The Mac regenerates the counterfactual images from the same seed instead of transferring them.
- Training: bf16 LoRA at about 10 GB VRAM for the 4B and about 22 GB for the 9B (Unsloth table); images capped at 768 px; gradient checkpointing; about 0.5-1.5 h per 4B run estimated, 7-8 runs. The server also runs bf16 evaluation of all 4B/9B arms on every test item.
- Estimated GPU rental: 4-5 days (11-07 to 11-11).
- API baselines: precomputed once by the student on a stratified subset of about 400 items (5 samples each, 2 providers, with a budget cap written in the plan), fully logged, never called at the booth.
