The student then has to write and own H1-H7 plus E1-E8 on the morning of 11-06. SFT launches that night, but the full physics review of the training families is not until 11-08, so any correction means retraining inside the 11-09 window. There is no Mac-side mlx-vlm training fallback. SCIENCE: the best-controlled design of the four: shuffled-label LoRA, a gradient-boosted-tree 'is an LM needed' baseline, a signature panel that levels arithmetic across arms, the L1-shift/L2/L3 transfer ladder, TOST no-harm checks and an adapter-effect positive control. That makes its upgrade claim the most defensible. Gaps: the referee grids only the error magnitude, so nuisance parameters (true k, mu) still need marginalising. vLLM's qwen3_5 class lists Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration and IsHybrid as bases, not SupportsLoRA, so serving LoRA through it is unconfirmed and merge-then-serve is the safe route. RISKIEST SINGLE STEP: the bf16 LoRA SFT of Qwen3.5-9B on the 5090 on the night of 11-06. It is the first contact with the sm_120 + transformers>=5.2 + flash-linear-attention/causal-conv1d stack, at a sequence length Unsloth's 22 GB figure does not state. Every E1-E7 result and the 11-09 adapter depend on that one time-boxed run.
fatal_flaws: The schedule closes only if nothing fails. SFT is a single <=4 h run on the night of 11-06, but the full physics review of the 18 training families is on 11-08, so any template correction forces a retrain inside the 11-09 product window.
No Mac-side (mlx-vlm) training fallback if the sm_120 Qwen3.5 stack fails on 11-06. The Qwen3.5-4B fallback runs on the same stack, so it fails the same way.

Pre-11-06 scope does not fit six AI-only days with tests: 24 families x 3-4 errors with menus, fixes and bilingual templates, plus the referee, harness, converter and full product rework. The student must also take ownership of H1-H7 and E1-E8 in a plan written in one morning.

scores.design: open-set-vision: CounterLab (counterfactual-tuned conformal experiment recognition, Qwen3.5-4B)
scores.justification: MEMORY: closes. The recognizer is the 4B (app about 7-8 GB, estimate), and the 27B runs alone under an MLX memory cap. It respects the upload, photo and adapter rules. DATA is where it fails. Recounting the label files in the repo snapshot: the 568 frames are 6 clips from only 3 source videos (about 332-337 friction frames from 2 videos, about 226 steel-ball frames from 1). The 242 photo labels (about 232 distinct shots plus 10 '_inv' duplicates) hold about 95 single-cart+track, about 23 two-cart and about 115 parts-only scenes, and no Hooke setups. So 'held-out source groups', the cluster bootstrap and a 90% +/- 3 pp conformal guarantee checked against the Beta law rest on a handful of non-exchangeable clusters. McNemar over about 1,000 correlated edits overstates n. The primary endpoint is tested on the same synthetic-inpainting distribution CET trains on; natural pairs (20-60) are only exploratory. PRODUCT HEADROOM is small. The rules already settle friction and two-cart scenes, the single-cart tie cannot be decided from pixels by construction, and physics.py's single-reading '<15% verified' path is left untouched. The novelty is real: matched-artifact counterfactual pairs, option dropout and physics-derived set labels. But the planned poster visuals use images that include frames of downloaded videos, with no licence check. RISKIEST SINGLE STEP: the first CET run on 11-07. It is a custom four-term-loss trainer (letter cross-entropy + symmetric KL + hinge vs matched controls + evidence target) on the Qwen3.5-4B VLM that cannot be GPU-tested beforehand. It starts only after the student's same-day labelling and group splits, and its adapter must then be converted, parity-tested and integrated, all on 11-09.
fatal_flaws: Too few independent source groups for group-held-out testing, a cluster bootstrap or the 90% +/- 3 pp conformal-coverage claim. There are 3 source videos (2 friction, 1 steel ball) plus a few EXIF photo sessions, and no Hooke setups. Effective n is far below the roughly 1,000 edited variants.
The primary endpoint (minimal-pair accuracy) uses the same synthetic-inpainting distribution CET is trained on. Real transfer (20-60 natural pairs) is only exploratory.
Little product gain by 11-09. The rules already settle friction and two-cart photos, the cart+track tie cannot be decided visually, and the single-reading analysis with the 15% rule stays unchanged.

A custom VLM loss trainer that cannot be GPU-tested before 11-07 and the student's same-day labelling both gate the first run. Adapter conversion, the parity test and the product freeze all land on 11-09.

scores.design: wow-product: Lab Sleuth (verifier-trained 9B, SFT then GRPO, sabotage bench)
scores.justification: Best product and booth of the four: suspect board, ghost curves, sabotage mode, paper sabotage cards. It also has the best sim-to-real evidence: a deliberately misspecified hi-fi simulator plus a real blinded sabotage bench. Inputs to the API baselines are synthetic only. MEMORY: closes; the product runs the 9B at about 9-11 GB (estimate), and the 27B runs alone. It respects the upload, photo and adapter rules. FEASIBILITY is weak. The 5090 is rented and bootstrapped only after signatures (the evening of 11-06), so kernel compiles and model downloads eat into the GPU window. The headline 'trained by RL' needs 9B bf16 GRPO inside 32 GB with Unsloth/HF generation. Unsloth's Qwen3.5 RL path requires fast_inference=False, and its Qwen3.5 guide links a GRPO notebook only for the 4B. The student also has to run 24-48 bench runs, each with two follow-ups, on top of the plan, forms, labelling and all the writing in 9 days. H1 (in-distribution vs untuned) is near-certain to pass and so tells little. Transfer (H3) rests on only 4 training experiments. The RFT and 4B fallbacks keep it alive. RISKIEST SINGLE STEP: the overnight GRPO run on 11-07 of Qwen3.5-9B (bf16 LoRA, groups of 6-8, <=320 tokens, HF generation; my estimate is 26-30 GB peak). An OOM, instability or a throughput shortfall there cuts the RL claim back to RFT, with one day left before the 11-09 freeze.
fatal_flaws: The headline RL claim depends on one overnight 9B bf16 GRPO run inside 32 GB, with generation through Unsloth/HF because the Qwen3.5 RL path disables vLLM, and Unsloth links a Qwen3.5 GRPO example only for the 4B. If it fails, the pitch falls back to RFT with one day left before the 11-09 freeze.

The student's workload does not fit 9 days: 24-48 bench runs, each with two follow-ups, plus the plan, forms, labels and all the writing. The confirmatory H4b fails by default if there is no lab access.

H1 compares an in-distribution fine-tune with untuned models on its own four training experiments, so it is near-certain to pass and adds little evidence. Transfer rests on only 4 training experiments.

scores.design: lead-concept: Lab Detective (engine-verified Qwen3.5-4B, identifiability atlas, EIG closed loop)
scores.justification: It wins on shippability and gives up little rigour. GPU risk is the lowest: the 4B bf16 LoRA needs about 10 GB VRAM, Unsloth's Qwen3.5 guide ships a 4B GRPO notebook, S1 and S2 take hours, and there is slack to absorb a one-day slip in the plan/forms signing on 11-06 (a bottleneck every design shares). E1-E3 (atlas, engine, EIG loop) are CPU-only and take about 1-2 h on the Mac on 11-07 (estimate), so a quantitative physics-education result exists even if every GPU job fails. MEMORY: the laptop tier (4B MLX 3.06 GB, app about 5-7 GB) fits far below 24 GB and suits 8 GB school laptops. Mac mlx-vlm SFT from engine traces is a real fallback. It also defers the 16 GB download to 11-06, uploads nothing, avoids LM Studio for adapters, and avoids measuring a human variable in the real runs (no stopwatch-based setups). Oracle-normalised transfer, unmodelled-fault and shuffled-row controls, and a verifier validated against a blinded audit make the upgrade claim defensible. WEAKNESSES: (a) the workstation tier puts the 27B next to Streamlit, YOLO and a browser at an estimated 20-23.5 GB, with no margin under a 24 GB cap and a 23 GB kill threshold; (b) S2 samples from the untuned base under a fixed threshold; (c) H1 is partly true by construction and only as good as the AI-written fault library, so it needs the sensitivity analysis; (d) eight hypotheses are too many for a plan the student writes on 11-06. RISKIEST SINGLE STEP: S2, the reward-filtered self-training sampled from the untuned 4B. Its acceptance rate under the pre-registered threshold is unknown until 11-07, and the primary endpoint (S2 vs base on held-out experiments) depends on it. Fix: run S2 as expert iteration from S1.
fatal_flaws: As specified, the workstation tier keeps the 27B (18.5-21 GB) loaded alongside Streamlit, YOLO and a browser: about 20-23.5 GB, inside the 24 GB cap only at the low end, so it would routinely trip the 23 GB watchdog in class. Fix: run the 27B as a batch-only baseline.

S2, the arm behind the primary endpoint, samples from the untuned 4B under a fixed pre-registered reward threshold. With low acceptance it cannot differ from base. Fix: expert iteration from S1, or pre-register S1 vs base as the primary comparison.

grafts: From LabSleuth (model-depth): a classical-ML baseline (gradient-boosted trees on the same code-computed signature features) to answer 'is a language model needed at all?'.

From LabSleuth: a shuffled-label LoRA negative control (same tasks, cause labels shuffled within each experiment), to show any gain comes from engine-verified labels rather than exposure to the output format.

From LabSleuth: cheap extra transfer rungs. (1) Experiment-cause pairs withheld from training and from the training candidate lists. (2) A shift split with heavier-tailed noise, coarser resolution and doubled timing noise. Each arm gets one pre-specified checkpoint, and the eval-set SHA-256 hashes are appended to the signed plan before training.

From LabSleuth: positive controls. (1) An arm with the oracle answer in the prompt, which must score about 100%. (2) A converter unit test on a tiny synthetic adapter, run before 11-06. (3) An adapter-effect check after PEFT-to-MLX conversion: the Mac adapter must change outputs wherever the server adapter does.

From LabSleuth: TOST equivalence ('must not change') checks after the text-only LoRA, on photo recognition over the people-screened image set and on a fixed 300-item PhyX (MIT-licensed) general-physics subset.

From LabSleuth: set up the 5090 environment before signatures, with no data (pinned CUDA >= 12.8 image, Gated-DeltaNet kernel compile). Measure throughput in each job's first 10 minutes and time-box every job.

From Lab Sleuth (wow-product): the deliberately misspecified hi-fi simulator as a test-only sim-to-real proxy split. It adds effects the engine never models: pulley inertia and friction, rolling resistance, air drag, string mass, ex-Gaussian timing noise and transcription slips.

From Lab Sleuth: at the booth, a judge challenge with paper sabotage cards (no QR codes). In the app, ghost-curve overlays of each top cause's prediction on the student's points, plus a quantitative fix-and-verify step that gives the fix and its predicted re-run result.

From Lab Sleuth: the student hand-codes one fault model himself (e.g. a Hooke ruler-zero offset) and checks it against the engine, as independence evidence for the interview. During the real runs he also measures how far the spring scale's zero shifts between vertical and horizontal use; the literature search found no value for it.

From Lab Sleuth: a closed vocabulary of signature types (y-offset, x-offset, slope scale, bend, scatter too large/small, drift, none), shared by the engine, the model output and the UI, as the explicit scaffold for transfer to held-out experiments.

From CounterLab (open-set-vision): restrict LoRA targets to the language-model linear layers whose names map one-to-one onto mlx-vlm's qwen3_5 implementation; vLLM packs in_proj_qkv+in_proj_z and in_proj_b+in_proj_a. Serve every local model through mlx_vlm.server from the folders lms downloaded, so there are no duplicate 16 GB copies, and logprobs and thinking-off are available by default.

From CounterLab: person screening with the COCO yolov8n.pt already in the project folder. Any image split is grouped by EXIF session or source video, with pHash de-duplication. The P1 minimal-pair test adds matched-artifact control masks.
must_cut: Lab Detective's workstation tier in the interactive product, i.e. the 27B loaded alongside Streamlit, YOLO and a browser (about 20-23.5 GB estimated). The 27B runs only as an overnight batch baseline with nothing else loaded.
S2 sampled from the untuned base as the primary-endpoint arm. Either sample S2 from S1 (expert iteration), or pre-register S1 vs base as the primary comparison.
S3 GRPO and the 9B scale point from the critical path to 11-14. They are P1, run only if S1 and S2 are finished and the GPU is idle; otherwise they move to December.
The 27B thinking-on arm and the NVFP4 27B server evaluation (vLLM NVFP4 on sm_120 is unverified). Use llama.cpp GGUF on the server or the Mac overnight run instead.

Hypotheses beyond about four confirmatory ones. Demote H2, H5, H7 and H8 to engineering criteria, controls or exploratory analyses, so the student can write and own the plan on 11-06 and the Holm-corrected family stays small.
The phase-2 vision counterfactual LoRA and the sympy generic-signature engine as November work. Keep them only as listed later phases of the plan.
Any 27B QLoRA, in every design: Unsloth advises against QLoRA for Qwen3.5, and transferring a bnb-4bit-trained adapter to the MLX affine 4-bit base is untested.
From CounterLab: the custom four-term CET trainer, and any in-domain conformal 'guarantee' claim resting on 3 source videos and a few photo sessions.
From LabSleuth: the 24-family LabSim, the family cross-validation folds and the parallel 4B tier, all before 11-14.
From Lab Sleuth: 9B GRPO as the headline, the 48-run bench target before 11-14 (cap it at 24) and the fault-parameterised 'experiment you actually ran' animation.
Any data from classroom use, from classmates or from teacher ratings without prior IRB approval, and any live API call in the product or at the booth.

scores.justification: Teacher view: the product side targets real lab misconceptions. It nudges for repeats and a varied independent variable, replaces the 15% rule with an uncertainty budget and a z verdict, adds a predict step and a detective card with one next measurement, and has a classroom mode that shows only referee results and checked templates. Its ML evaluation is the most rigorous of the four: a shared signature panel levels out arithmetic, and it adds a shuffled-label LoRA, a classical-ML probe ('is an LLM needed at all?'), in-context and no-panel controls, TOST no-harm checks and eval hashes fixed before training. But the research moves to 24 synthetic families (Ohm, Snell, Boyle, calorimetry, thin lens and more) with roughly 80 AI-drafted fault models, many with priors tagged 'assumption'. The student can check only the six curriculum families before SFT. The same unchecked referee then grades the model, so a physics mistake can never show up in the metrics, and he cannot defend the non-mechanics families in the 25-point interview. Held-out-family 'transfer' partly comes down to matching panel signatures against a shared error-pattern list; the GBT probe may match the LLM. That is honest, but it weakens the upgrade story. 'Physics is the only teacher' and 'exact referee' overstate what is really an AI-drafted simulator with Monte Carlo EIG. The plan is written in one morning and the AI runs the pre-registered analysis, both Rule 8 risks. Weakest feasibility of the four.
fatal_flaws: Physics breadth the student cannot verify in time: about 80 AI-drafted fault models across 24 families (optics, electricity and thermal included), most priors tagged 'assumption'. Only the six curriculum families get checked before SFT. The same unchecked referee labels the training data and grades every arm, so template errors are invisible in the results, and the student cannot defend most families in the interview. As scheduled for 11-14 the ground truth is effectively AI-authored.

scores.justification: Clever ML: matched-artifact counterfactual pairs, option dropout to train a 'not listed' answer, group-aware conformal sets checked against their theoretical Beta law, and a data-matched SFT control with two seeds. It is the most direct answer to the 'recognise any experiment' wish and the closest continuation of the 809-image work. Its 'What will you measure?' question for the cart+track tie is a nice touch. As a teacher I rate its classroom value lowest. Students do not struggle to know which experiment they are doing; the teacher assigns it. physics.py's single-reading '<15% = verified' logic is left unchanged, so nothing addresses systematic versus random error, single readings or what to measure next, and there is no classroom closed loop. The data cannot carry the claims. There are 3 source videos and a few photo sessions, Hooke is absent, and average speed, Newton-2 and energy share one cart+track look. Held-out-group results therefore rest on a handful of independent scenes, and exchangeability is doubtful. The line shown to students, '90% guaranteed... calibrated on photos like yours', overclaims coverage that is only marginal. The design trains on, and plans to display, frames from online videos whose provenance is unchecked. Its custom four-term VLM loss is the riskiest code path, and students will find it dull.
fatal_flaws: It solves a problem students do not have and leaves the one they do have untouched. The experiment is assigned by the teacher; physics.py's single-reading '<15% = verified' rule stays; there is no help with systematic error or the next measurement, and no classroom closed loop.

Its central claims rest on very few independent scenes: 3 source videos plus a few photo sessions, Hooke absent, and three experiments sharing one cart+track appearance. Held-out-group minimal-pair accuracy and in-domain conformal coverage cannot be established with useful confidence.

It tells students a set is 'guaranteed' and 'calibrated on photos like yours'. The coverage is marginal and rests on exchangeability, so the claim is false in a new classroom until the set is recalibrated.

scores.justification: The best classroom idea of the four. 'A wrong result is an accurate measurement of a slightly different experiment' replaces 'human error' with physics. The suspect library matches faults I actually see: friction unbalanced or over-balanced, m not << M, a spring scale zeroed vertically and then used horizontally, distance measured nose-to-tail, pendulum length to the top of the bob, and v computed from sqrt(2gh), which makes data 'too perfect'. Ghost overlays, predicted outcomes shown before measuring (predict-observe-explain), a quantitative fix-and-verify loop, sabotage practice and paper judge cards will engage 14-17-year-olds and judges alike. Compliance is careful: Path A/B, scripted mode, reaction-time and elastic-limit faults simulated only, Form 3, one fault model hand-coded by the student, and only synthetic inputs sent to the APIs. Weaknesses: (1) The posterior is closed-world: it always names one of 4-6 suspects and has no 'none of these'. (2) The model gets no levelled feature panel, so any gain may just be arithmetic. (3) There is no negative training control, and the student knows each planted bench fault. (4) Two of the three held-out experiments (momentum, energy) are ones the product's engines already cover, not the 'other' experiments the model is actually deployed for. (5) GRPO on the hybrid 9B as a P0 item, plus the heaviest UX build, strain the 11-09 date. (6) The pitch says the reasoning comes from the 9B, when the engine produces the curriculum diagnoses. (7) It overuses the word 'exact'.
fatal_flaws: Closed-world diagnosis. The posterior is always forced onto one of 4-6 listed suspects or Just Noise, with no out-of-model check. Any real unmodelled fault (pulley friction, a digit slip, two faults at once) gets a confident wrong culprit. That is harmful on real classroom data and contradicts the design's own honesty goals. It is fatal for classroom use unless a posterior-predictive 'not in my list' check is grafted in.

scores.justification: The best overall base for a project that has to work both in class and at ISEF. Its primary science is an identifiability atlas: what the single-reading protocol and the standard worksheet can reveal at all, and which one extra measurement resolves each confused pair. That is a real physics-education result, and it survives if training fails. It quantifies the old app's single-reading limit, which gives a strong continuation story, and it hands teachers an actionable protocol view. It is honest by design: 'cause not in my list', 'your data cannot tell yet', bracketed thresholds, a 'no upgrade' outcome stated in advance, and accuracy reported as a fraction of the Bayes-optimal oracle. The worked energy example is correct and derivable on a whiteboard: the ratios sin theta, 1 - mu cot theta, 5/7 and k^2 are separated by one change of angle. The steel-ball booth story is truthful. The 4B upgrade is cheap, feasible and relevant to school laptops. Transfer is tested on the 'other' experiments the model would actually serve (near transfer, so a success is modest). Real runs use sealed cards and avoid stopwatch-only setups; lessons stay teacher-run and scripted; SRC rulings are requested in writing. Needs fixing: (1) H7's row shuffle removes no information, because each (x, y) pair stays intact. (2) S2 is sampled from the weak base and may yield few accepted traces. (3) The real-run EIG-versus-repeat test needs both follow-ups measured on every run. (4) The 27B workstation tier sits at the 24 GB cap. (5) The AI briefing pack's 'list of primary sources' is a starter bibliography, which ISEF forbids. (6) It is less playful than Lab Sleuth (wow-product).

grafts: From Lab Sleuth (wow-product): the suspect board, where each card shows a friendly name, the physics name, the data signature it predicts and a live posterior bar. Add ghost best-fit curves over the student's points, show each suspect's predicted value BEFORE the student measures, and let the student type an optional prediction first (predict-observe-explain).

From Lab Sleuth (wow-product): a fix-and-verify loop. Give a quantitative fix (e.g. raise the far end about 1.1 cm) with a predicted re-run result that either confirms the culprit or reopens the case. This makes the curriculum's 'propose ways to reduce errors' testable.

From Lab Sleuth (wow-product): a sabotage practice mode, where the software plants a hidden fault in a virtual run and students hunt it with the fewest measurements, plus the 12 paper sabotage cards for the booth Judge Challenge (offline, no QR codes).

From Lab Sleuth (wow-product): the deliberately misspecified hi-fi simulator (pulley inertia and friction, rolling resistance, drag, string mass, ex-Gaussian timing, digit slips) as the sim-to-real stress world. Also add the 'too-perfect data' suspect (scatter below instrument noise, e.g. v computed from sqrt(2gh)), worded without accusation.

From Lab Sleuth (wow-product): in every real run, measure both the EIG-chosen follow-up and a plain repeat, in random order, so the real-data EIG-versus-repeat test is paired. Also measure how far the school spring scales' zero shifts between vertical and horizontal use, which has no literature value.

From Lab Sleuth (wow-product): the student hand-codes one fault model (Hooke ruler-zero offset) and checks it against the engine, as independence evidence for the interview. Add a teacher 'assessment mode' that shows the evidence but hides the verdict.

From LabSleuth (model-depth): a shuffled-label LoRA negative control (cause labels permuted within each experiment); a classical-ML probe (gradient-boosted trees on the same signature features) to answer 'is a language model needed at all?'; and the no-feature ablation run on the trained arms as well as the base models.

From LabSleuth (model-depth): TOST equivalence margins for what the upgrade must not change (photo recognition and a fixed general-physics set), a leakage checker that must catch a planted duplicate, and one pre-specified checkpoint per arm, with eval-set hashes appended to the signed plan before training.

From CounterLab (open-set-vision), for the P1 recognition path: matched-artifact controls for the minimal pairs (the same mask and fill applied to background); source-grouped conformal calibration with plain-language UI wording and no 'guaranteed'; a teacher recalibration page using about 30 labelled photos; 'What will you measure?' as the clarifying question for the cart+track tie; and a blind re-label of 20% of the photos a day later for intra-rater kappa.

From CounterLab (open-set-vision) and Lab Sleuth (wow-product): screen every image with the existing COCO person detector. Use the 25-photo set only if the student took the photos himself and they contain no classmates' data, or if they are certified de-identified. Check the provenance of the 3 source videos before any frame appears on the board.

Fixes inside Lab Detective: replace H7's row shuffle with a permutation of the measured column (or a table swapped in from another case); seed the S2 rejection sampling from S1 (expert iteration), or pre-register that the primary arm is chosen on validation data; write 'Bayes-optimal under our simulator's assumptions' instead of 'exact'; and in IRB and consent documents call the feature 'error-source analysis', not 'diagnosis'.
must_cut: The 'list of primary sources to locate and read' in the AI-made briefing pack (Lab Detective). AI must not supply a starter bibliography; the student runs his own literature search and verifies every source.

The live workstation tier that runs the 27B alongside Streamlit, YOLO and a browser at an estimated 20-23.5 GB. Keep the 27B only as an overnight baseline loaded alone, and ship the product on the 4B (9B optional).
H7 'shuffled rows' as written: row order carries no information except drift, so it cannot test whether the decisions use the data.

Any classroom session run by the student; any data or observations from the lessons from 11-07 on; and any design change made from watching classmates use the app. Also no teacher ratings, and no 'anonymous cause-count export' feature (from LabSleuth (model-depth)).
The 24-family breadth (optics, electricity and thermal families) from the 11-14 path. Stay in mechanics, where the student can verify and defend every fault model.
CounterLab's custom CET trainer from the 11-14 path, and any 'guaranteed 90%' or 'calibrated on photos like yours' wording on screens that students see.
GRPO on the 9B as a P0 item, and the fault-parameterised 'experiment you actually ran' animation. GRPO stays P1 on the 4B, and the ghost overlays carry the same message.
All P2 items from the 11-14 path (vision-side counterfactual LoRA, the sympy law compiler, 27B QLoRA, video, hidden-state probes). They stay in the plan only as later phases.

Presenting the earlier five classroom sessions or the 24/25-photo result as ISEF results. Showing free-generated AI text to anyone other than the student researcher during the ISEF window. The AI launching formal runs or running the analysis in place of the student.

design.name: Lab Detective: engine-trained, fully offline diagnosis of systematic error in school mechanics labs, and the one measurement that settles it (continuation of Physics Pictorial Recognition)
design.one_line_pitch: A 'wrong' lab result is usually an accurate measurement of a slightly different experiment. Lab Detective is a fully offline lab partner that works out which hidden cause best explains a student's mechanics data (unbalanced friction, a mis-zeroed spring scale, a spinning ball), says plainly when the data cannot tell, and names the one extra measurement that would settle it. The Bayesian physics engine behind it also trains a 4-billion-parameter vision-language model with no human or API labels, and the project measures how much of that skill transfers to experiments the model never saw, as a fraction of the Bayes-optimal limit.
design.research_question: How close can a laptop-sized vision-language model, fine-tuned only on tasks labelled by a Bayesian physics engine and run fully offline, come to the Bayes-optimal limit set by the measurement protocol in naming the systematic cause behind school mechanics data and choosing the most informative next measurement, on experiments held out from training?
hypotheses_or_criteria: RULE FOR EVERY LINE BELOW: bracketed numbers are proposals. The student restates each claim in his own words, chooses the final numbers and commits them in his signed research plan. The frozen test-set SHA-256 hashes are appended to the plan, dated, before any training or evaluation. Each arm has one pre-specified checkpoint. 'Bayes-optimal' always means 'Bayes-optimal under our simulator's assumptions'. A miss is reported as a miss.

C1 - CONFIRMATORY, SCIENCE (identifiability atlas, E1). Under each curriculum experiment's standard multi-point worksheet (as written in the student's textbook), simulated with literature-calibrated noise, at least one pair of modelled causes is robustly confounded in at least [4] of the 6 experiments. Robustly confounded means pairwise Bayes-optimal accuracy < [0.6] in all four sensitivity settings (fault-size priors x0.5 and x2; noise x0.5 and x2). For each confounded pair, one extra measurement from the menu lifts pairwise Bayes accuracy to >= [0.8]. Falsified if fewer than [4] experiments have a robust confound, or if some confound cannot be resolved by any single menu measurement. The old app's single-reading protocol is reported descriptively only, because its failure is nearly certain.

C2 - CONFIRMATORY, CLOSED LOOP (E3, E5). One extra measurement chosen by expected information gain (EIG) raises the engine posterior of the true cause more than one repeat of the last measurement, which is what students usually do. (a) Simulation: 840 closed-loop cases whose extra measurements come from the hi-fi simulator (it contains effects the engine never models), paired Wilcoxon signed-rank, alpha 0.05; the same test on labsim is reported as an in-model check. (b) Real apparatus: the student's own sealed fault-injection runs, where BOTH follow-ups are measured in every run in script-randomised order, paired Wilcoxon, n >= [24] runs. If fewer than [24] real runs exist at the analysis freeze, (b) is reported as pending and completed in Phase 2 with the same method.

C3 - CONFIRMATORY, PRIMARY ML (E4). On the 6 held-out experiments (720 cases), the engine-trained Qwen3.5-4B (S1, engine-target SFT) beats the untuned Qwen3.5-4B on top-1 cause accuracy (exact McNemar, two-sided alpha 0.05). Both arms get the identical prompt contract, experiment card, code-computed signature panel, candidate causes written as plain physical descriptions with no signature tags, JSON schema, greedy decoding and 512-token budget. The gain is also reported as a fraction of the engine's Bayes-optimal accuracy on the same cases, with an experiment-level cluster bootstrap. C3 is read as 'learned from engine labels' only if the shuffled-label LoRA control gains < [2] pp over the base on the same cases.

SECONDARY FAMILY (pre-registered, Holm-corrected, none is a headline claim). S-a transfer ladder, S1 vs base, on in-distribution, noise-shift, withheld-cause and hi-fi sets; pre-registered accuracy drop from in-distribution to hi-fi <= [10] pp. S-b S2 (expert iteration seeded from S1) vs S1 on the held-out experiments. S-c lower normalised EIG-regret of the model's next-measurement choice for S1 than base (Wilcoxon). S-d better calibration for S1 than base (Brier score, 15-bin ECE), and a false-alarm rate on clean data <= [10]%. S-e the best 4B is non-inferior to the untuned Qwen3.8-27B on a stratified 800-case subset (margin [3] pp) while using <= 1/4 of its peak memory. S-f verifier-flagged unsupported claims are <= [5]% for the tuned 4B and fewer than for both base models (McNemar); the verifier reaches precision >= [0.9] and recall >= [0.8] against the student's blinded audit. S-g on held-out experiments, S1 predicts each candidate cause's signature type more accurately than base; this is the mechanism of transfer. S-h engine honesty: >= [70]% of unmodelled faults are flagged 'cause not in my list'.

CONTROLS THAT MUST PASS BEFORE ANY RESULT IS INTERPRETED. K1 the oracle-in-prompt arm scores >= [98]%, showing the harness and parser work. K2 the leakage checker catches a planted duplicate. K3 swapped-table control: each case keeps its label but gets the data table of another case of the same experiment, and every arm must fall to within [5] pp of chance. This shows decisions come from the data, and replaces the earlier row-shuffle idea, since row order carries no information. K4 adapter-effect check: the converted Mac adapter changes the output on >= [90]% of the parity cases where the server adapter changed it. K5 no-panel ablation run on both base and S1, reporting what the levelling tool itself contributes.

WHAT THE UPGRADE MUST NOT CHANGE (TOST equivalence: the 90% CI of the paired difference must lie inside the margin). (1) The 4B's photo recognition on the people-screened, provenance-cleared image set plus the external CC set, within +/-[5] pp. (2) A fixed 300-item PhyX subset (MIT licence) of general physics, within +/-[3] pp.

ENGINEERING CRITERIA (pass/fail). EC1: every function works with networking off, and no external API is called inside the product. EC2: the product stack peaks at <= [8] GB; everything we run together never exceeds 24 GB (watchdog log); the 27B baseline, run alone, peaks at <= [22] GB. EC3, latency on the M4 Pro: engine diagnosis < 1 s; 4B diagnosis plus explanation median <= [15] s; photo recognition <= [10] s per photo of <= 1024 px. EC4: >= 99% of outputs are schema-valid. EC5: manual selection of the six curriculum experiments is reachable in <= 2 clicks from every screen and is never overridden. EC6: >= 95% identical top-1 between the server bf16 adapter and the Mac 4-bit build on 200 parity cases. EC7: the fixed 'relative error < 15% = verified' rule is gone everywhere, replaced by an uncertainty-normalised z agreement.

EXPLORATORY (no confirmatory claim). (1) Fix-and-verify predictions on >= [6] real runs. (2) The measured zero shift of the school's spring scales between vertical and horizontal use; the literature search found no value for it. (3) Near- vs far-transfer breakdown per held-out experiment. (4) P1 recognition results (candidate sets, one clarifying question, minimal pairs), reported per source group as small-n.
design.product_experience:
STUDENT (laptop tier, fully offline; Chinese UI with an English toggle for the booth)
1. Open Lab Detective with networking off. There are two doors: 'Pick my experiment' or 'Identify from photo'. The six curriculum experiments are one click away on every screen, and a manual choice is never overridden.
2. Photo path.
- YOLO draws boxes and the student corrects them on the existing canvas. The existing rules decide when they can.
- On a tie or an unknown setup, the local 4B model sees the photo, downscaled to <= 1024 px, with numbered boxes. It returns one of the six experiments or 'other: <name>', plus the cues it used ('string over a pulley to a hanging mass', 'track tilted').
- The proven cart+track tie is settled by one question: 'What will you measure? Time over a marked distance / acceleration with a hanging weight / speed at the bottom of the slope.'
- P1: a small candidate set is shown instead of a single guess.
3. 'Other experiment'. The app says it has no physics model for '<name>'. The student picks the variables and the expected relation from a short menu: proportional, linear, inverse, square or power (P1: pre-filled from the photo). Code computes the same signature panel used everywhere, and the tuned model proposes suspects and a next measurement. Every later output is labelled 'AI estimate - not physics-verified'.
4. Predict first (optional, predict-observe-explain). The student taps the suspect he expects. The choice stays on the device.
5. Enter a multi-point table, e.g. extension for 5 loads, acceleration for 5 hanging masses, or final speed for 3 heights. Instrument resolutions come pre-filled from the teacher's profile. A single reading is still accepted, with a note that one point cannot separate suspects.
6. Agreement meter, e.g. 'k = 24.1 +/- 0.6 N/m; z = 2.4: in tension'.
- Bands: consistent / in tension / inconsistent.
- The relative error is still shown, but the fixed 15% rule is gone.
7. Suspect board: 4-6 cards plus 'Just noise' and 'Cause not in my list'.
- Each card shows a friendly name, the physics name, the data signature it predicts and a live probability bar, e.g. 'Sticky track = friction not balanced: the a-F line crosses below zero'.
- Ghost curves: each top suspect's best-fit curve is drawn through the student's points.
8. One-more-measurement card.
- It names the single most informative next measurement and its lab minutes.
- Before the student measures, it shows each top suspect's predicted result ('Sticky track: about 0.35 m/s^2; Heavy hanger: about 0.52 m/s^2'). He may type his own prediction first.
- He measures, enters the value and the bars move, for up to 3 rounds.
- If no measurement on the menu can separate the last suspects, the app says so and explains why.
9. Verdict and fix-and-verify.
- The culprit is shown with a size interval, a quantitative fix and the predicted re-run result ('after re-zeroing, the intercept should be 0 +/- 0.03 N').
- The re-run either confirms the culprit or reopens the case.
10. Explanation.
- Up to 120 words, written by the local model from the engine's fact sheet.
- Every number, unit, direction word and named cause is checked. The model gets one rewrite; after that a fixed template is used.
- In scripted mode only templates appear.
- Curated 'how to reduce this error' tips follow, matching the curriculum requirement to analyse errors and propose ways to reduce them.
11. Export the table, plots, verdict and the deciding measurement into his own report.

TEACHER
1. Once: set instrument profiles (spring-scale division and range, ruler, cart mass, track length, photogate flag width). Per lesson: choose the experiments and switch off causes that do not apply to the school's kit. The 'speed computed from the height' method check is off by default.
2. Scripted mode (template text only) is the default and is required for every lesson. Assessment mode (P1) shows the evidence and probability bars but hides the verdict.
3. Protocol view (P1): a heat map from the atlas of which causes today's worksheet cannot tell apart, plus the one protocol change that fixes most of them (e.g. 'add a zero-hanging-mass run').
4. Fault-library viewer: each cause's physics, data signature, noise model and source.
5. Practice challenge (P1): the software plants a hidden fault in a virtual run, and groups find it with the fewest measurements.
6. Lessons are ordinary teaching. Nothing is logged or collected, and nothing enters the ISEF project unless a later IRB-approved study runs (Phase 3).

JUDGES AT THE BOOTH (English build, offline, frozen)
1. Judge Challenge (P1).
- The judge draws one of 12 paper sabotage cards and picks a fault size.
- The hi-fi simulator, which contains effects the engine never models, produces a realistic data table.
- Lab Detective, on the 4B laptop tier, must name the culprit within 3 extra measurements, or say which pair it cannot separate and which measurement would.
- Precomputed scenarios are the fallback.
2. The spinning ball.
- The old app said 'error 29%, not verified', and the student blamed friction.
- Lab Detective shows that friction, rotation, slant length used as height and a flag-width error all fit the data at one angle. It asks for one run at a different angle; the ratio does not change, so rotation wins.
- Measuring the ball and the rail gap then explains why the share of energy in translation is even below 5/7.
3. Poster figures: the atlas heat maps, the transfer ladder as a fraction of the oracle, and the paired real-run result.

technical_components.name: labsim: executable physics twins of 12 mechanics experiments with curriculum fault libraries
technical_components.what:
- numpy forward models of each measurement protocol. All share one closed signature vocabulary: y-offset, x-offset, slope scale, bend at high x, scatter too large, scatter too small, drift with trial order, none.
- Training experiments (the six in the app's registry): friction, average speed, Hooke's law, Newton-2 with hanging mass, momentum with two carts, energy on an incline.
- Held-out experiments, used only as graders and never in training. Classified in advance as near transfer: inclined-plane friction, Atwood machine, free fall. Far transfer: simple pendulum g, horizontal projectile, lever balance.
- Each experiment has 4-6 causes, always including 'random error only'. Every cause carries a plain physical description, a signature tag, a fix and a source tag ('literature' or 'assumption'). Examples:
  - Newton-2: friction not balanced or over-balanced; hanging mass not << cart mass, with relative error (m+m_e)/M; string not parallel to the track.
  - Hooke: total length recorded instead of extension; hanger mass omitted; ruler zero offset; beyond the elastic limit.
  - Friction: scale zeroed vertically then used horizontally; upward pull angle; accelerating pull.
  - Energy: slant length used as height; rolling friction; flag-width error; rotational energy. A solid ball on a flat surface keeps 5/7 of the energy as translation; on two rails the contact radius r < R lowers this to 1/(1 + (2/5)(R/r)^2). Also a 'speed computed from the height' circular-method check, off by default and enabled by the teacher.
  - Momentum: track not level; friction between the gates; mass mis-entry; common flag-width scale.
  - Average speed: distance measured front-to-rear; cart not released from rest; slope too steep for manual timing.
- One cause per training experiment is withheld from training and from the training candidate lists. This is the 'new cause in a known experiment' rung.
- Noise uses literature values where they exist: manual start-stop interval N(0, 0.10^2 s^2); single-action bias 0.11 s with sd 0.07 s; resolution d/sqrt(12); ruler +/-1 mm; a photogate-bias case of about 5.7%. Where no value exists (spring-scale zero shift, parallax), a wide prior is used and flagged 'assumption'.
- Menus of 3-6 feasible extra measurements per experiment, each with estimated lab minutes and a simulated outcome.
- A one-page physics card per cause (formula, signature derivation, source tag) is generated from the code for the student's review.
technical_components.novelty_vs_prior_art: The physics of each cause comes from textbooks or teacher literature (e.g. He 2016 on (m+m_e)/M; Kok & Priemer 2023 on rotational energy) and is not claimed as new. The verified search found no executable, tested library of systematic-error hypotheses with literature noise for school mechanics experiments that serves as the shared ground truth for diagnosis, protocol audit and model training. CNKI was not searched systematically; the student checks it before claiming novelty.
technical_components.feasibility_and_memory:
- Pure numpy, < 0.5 GB, milliseconds per simulated dataset.
- About 1.5k lines (estimate), written by the coding assistant 10-31..11-03.
- Seconds-long analytic unit tests: zero-fault data must recover the ideal law, and large faults must show the hand-derived signature.
- Independent checks:
  - the second assistant re-implements the Newton-2 and energy forward models and one two-cause EIG case from the written physics spec (a differential test, logged);
  - the student reviews every training-experiment physics card on 11-07, before training;
  - the student hand-codes one fault model himself (Hooke ruler-zero offset).
- Mechanics only, so every cause can be derived on a whiteboard in the interview.

technical_components.name: Bayesian diagnosis engine with an honest 'cause not in my list'
technical_components.what:
- Computes a posterior over {random error only, cause_1..cause_K, none of these}.
- Marginal likelihoods: closed form (Bayesian linear-Gaussian) when a fault is linear in its parameters (offsets, scale factors); grid quadrature otherwise.
- Nuisance parameters (true k, mu, g-scale, cart mass) are marginalised on grids with weakly informative priors.
- A posterior-predictive misfit statistic, calibrated on simulation to a fixed false-alarm rate of [5%], triggers 'cause not in my list'.
- Uncertainty-normalised agreement z = (measured - predicted) / combined standard uncertainty. Proposed bands: consistent |z| < 2, in tension 2-3, inconsistent > 3. The classic relative error is still shown.
- Emits a fact sheet for the explainer, the verifier and the UI: numbers, units, signs, top causes, counterfactual ghost curves, the fix and the predicted re-run value.
- Registry v2 replaces physics.py's single-reading forms with multi-point tables and instrument profiles; single readings are still accepted.
technical_components.novelty_vs_prior_art: The methods are classical: model-based diagnosis (de Kleer & Williams 1987), model discrimination (Box & Hill 1967), Bayesian model comparison in intro labs (Blais 2020). New is automatic, real-time use over a curriculum fault library, evaluated against an oracle and on real runs. Replacing pass/fail with an uncertainty-normalised comparison follows physics-education arguments the student should find and read for himself.
technical_components.feasibility_and_memory:
- Vectorised numpy on the CPU; estimate 1-10 ms per diagnosis and < 0.3 GB; runs inside the product on the Mac.
- Unit tests: planted-fault recovery, posterior normalisation and an Occam check.
- Written 11-02.

technical_components.name: Expected-information-gain advisor and closed loop
technical_components.what:
- For each menu item, a Monte Carlo EIG on the posterior over causes (about 100-256 simulated outcomes), optionally per lab minute.
- It recommends the best item, says which suspects that item separates, and shows each top suspect's predicted outcome before the student measures.
- It takes the new reading, updates the posterior and repeats for up to 3 rounds. When no menu item can separate the remaining suspects, it says so plainly.
- A simulated-student loop drives E3, comparing EIG, EIG per minute, repeat, random choice and a fixed textbook extension.
- Real-run support for E5: every run records BOTH the EIG follow-up and a plain repeat, in an order taken from a committed random schedule.
- The same code picks the single clarifying question in recognition (P1).
technical_components.novelty_vs_prior_art: Choosing measurements by EIG is old (GDE 1987; BOED reviews; NIST optbayesexpt 2021), and BoxingGym (2025) reports that LLMs struggle at EIG-style design. Not found: EIG advice for school mechanics labs, tested in a real physical closed loop against students' usual default of repeating the same measurement.
technical_components.feasibility_and_memory: Estimate 0.1-1 s per recommendation on the CPU; negligible memory. Written 11-02.

technical_components.name: Identifiability atlas: the Bayes-optimal limit of school protocols
technical_components.novelty_vs_prior_art: Not found in the literature searched. This is the project's physics-education result, and it stands even if the ML part fails.
technical_components.feasibility_and_memory: Estimate 1-3 CPU-hours with 4 workers on the Mac, < 2 GB, run on 11-07 while no model is loaded. Before 11-06 it runs only at debug size (n = 20 per cell), with outputs discarded.

technical_components.name: Signature panel and closed signature vocabulary (the levelling tool)
technical_components.novelty_vs_prior_art: Standard statistics used in a tool-integrated-reasoning pattern (PAL, ToRA). Not claimed as new; its role is to make the comparisons fair.
technical_components.feasibility_and_memory: numpy, milliseconds. About 300 lines (estimate), written 11-03.

technical_components.name: Engine-verified fine-tuning of Qwen3.5-4B: S1 engine-target SFT plus the shuffled-label control (the model upgrade)
technical_components.what:
- Adapter: bf16 LoRA, r=16, alpha=32, dropout 0.05, on language-model linear layers whose PEFT names map one-to-one to mlx-vlm's qwen3_5 modules. Start with full-attention q/k/v/o and MLP gate/up/down; add the Gated-DeltaNet projections only if the converter's name-map test passes.
- Frozen: vision tower, embeddings, lm_head. Non-thinking chat format; loss on assistant tokens only.
- Input: experiment card; candidate causes as plain physical descriptions, with no signature tags; data table of 1-8 rows (single readings included); signature panel; measurement menu.
- Output JSON: short evidence; the data's signature; each cause's signature type and probability; p(none of these); the next measurement with the expected result under the top two causes; the z verdict; an explanation of <= 80 words, in Chinese or English (50/50).
- 20% of examples are cause-proposal tasks: propose up to 6 causes as (variable, signature type, description).
- S1 targets are written by the engine: posterior rounded to 0.05, the argmax-EIG item, the true signature tags, and a templated explanation with 3 paraphrases per slot.
- Anti-shortcut measures: cause IDs and their order randomised; magnitude priors overlap.
- Shuffled-label control: identical prompts, steps and seed, with cause labels permuted within each experiment.
- Each run is time-boxed to <= 2 h; the example count is set from throughput measured in the first 10 minutes.
technical_components.feasibility_and_memory:
- RTX 5090: bf16 LoRA of the 4B needs about 10 GB VRAM per Unsloth's Qwen3.5 table. The table does not state a sequence length, so this is verified in the first run. bf16 avoids Unsloth's warning against QLoRA for this family.
- Estimates: S1 1-2 h; the control 1-2 h, run in the evening.
- Adapter about 65 MB (estimate).
- Tooling: Unsloth, falling back to ms-swift, then plain PEFT/TRL.
- If the sm_120 stack fails, a reduced S1 is trained overnight on the Mac with mlx-vlm (estimate 6-10 GB, never alongside the 27B).

technical_components.name: S2 expert iteration seeded from S1 (S3 GRPO later)
technical_components.what:
- Merge S1 into the bf16 base, then sample 8 answers per prompt (temperature 0.8) on about 3k fresh training-experiment prompts.
- Sampling uses vLLM serving the merged model, because vLLM LoRA support for qwen3_5 is unconfirmed; batched HF generate is the fallback.
- Reward R = format gate x (0.5 x (1 - 0.5 x ||p - q||^2) + 0.3 x EIG(chosen)/max EIG + 0.2 x verifier pass with coverage), where q is the engine posterior.
- Keep the best sample if R >= a pre-registered threshold, then train one SFT epoch continuing from S1.
- S3, GRPO on the same reward with a KL penalty to S2, is P2. It runs only if S1, S2 and all controls are finished and the GPU is idle before 11-10; otherwise it moves to Phase 2.
- Deployment rule (pre-registered, not a claim): the product ships S2 only if it beats S1 by >= [1] pp top-1 on the in-distribution validation split with no faithfulness regression. Otherwise it ships S1.
technical_components.novelty_vs_prior_art: Expert iteration / rejection-sampling fine-tuning (Yuan 2023; STaR, Zelikman 2022) with a bounded proper-scoring term (RLCR) and an engine-computed EIG term. The controlled SFT-vs-RFT comparison on held-out experiments tests the 'RL generalises, SFT memorises' prediction (Chu et al., ICML 2025) in a measurement-diagnosis domain.
technical_components.feasibility_and_memory: Estimate 1-2 h of sampling plus 1 h of SFT on the 5090 (the merged 4B in bf16 is about 9 GB, plus KV cache). Seeding from S1 rather than the untuned base fixes the low-acceptance risk the judges found.

technical_components.name: Hi-fi misspecified simulator (test-only sim-to-real proxy)
technical_components.what:
- Adds effects the engine never models: pulley inertia and friction, rolling resistance, air drag, string mass, ex-Gaussian (skewed) timing noise and occasional transcription slips.
- Produces a frozen 300-case robustness split, with a pre-registered accuracy drop measured against in-distribution.
- Supplies the outcomes of the closed-loop continuations in C2a, so EIG is tested under misspecification.
- Also feeds the booth Judge Challenge tables and the practice mode.
technical_components.novelty_vs_prior_art: A deliberate physics gap between the training world and the test world is a stronger proxy than noise-only misspecification. It is not claimed as a new method.
technical_components.feasibility_and_memory: numpy extensions of labsim, about 300 lines (estimate), written by the assistants on 11-06. The student generates the set, freezes it and hashes it before any model is evaluated on it.

technical_components.name: Evaluation harness: pre-registration, levelled baselines, controls, statistics, logs
technical_components.what:
- Seeded test sets are regenerated identically on the Mac and the server. Their SHA-256 hashes are compared and appended, dated, to the signed plan before any training; the files themselves are never uploaded.
- A leakage checker must catch a planted duplicate.
- One prompt contract for all arms: same card, candidates, panel and schema (constrained decoding where supported), greedy decoding, 512 new tokens. Thinking is off for local arms; API arms use their lowest reasoning setting (logged).
- Controls: oracle-in-prompt, swapped-table, unmodelled faults (two causes at once; a x10 transcription slip), clean data, and large obvious faults.
- Non-LLM references: gradient-boosted trees on panel features that predict the data signature, and a 20-line rule matcher. Both are given the oracle cause-signature tags.
- Statistics: exact McNemar; Wilcoxon signed-rank; Wilson and Clopper-Pearson intervals; paired and experiment-level cluster bootstrap (10,000 resamples); TOST; Holm; mixed-effects logistic regression as a sensitivity analysis; Brier; ECE with reliability diagrams; AUROC.
- Every local and API prompt and response is logged as JSONL with model id, build, settings and timestamp.
- Formal-run launcher: only the student starts formal runs. It asks for his name, writes a dated notebook stub, and refuses to run if the plan hash is missing.
technical_components.novelty_vs_prior_art: Method, not novelty. It follows the measurement-first discipline of the Gewu paper the student studied: criteria fixed before runs, baselines levelled on grader, budget, tool and prompt, and positive controls. That paper reports a naive gain of about +22 pp falling to about +2 pp once levelled, which is why levelling is built in from the start.
technical_components.feasibility_and_memory: CPU-light. About 800 lines (estimate), written 11-04.

technical_components.name: Fact-sheet explainer, claim verifier and scripted mode
technical_components.what:
- For registered experiments, the local model writes <= 120 words, using only the engine fact sheet.
- In open-set mode it writes from its own JSON, and the text is labelled 'AI estimate - not physics-verified'.
- A rule-based verifier (Chinese and English) extracts every number with its unit, every direction word (larger/smaller, 偏大/偏小), the named cause and the recommended measurement, and checks each against the fact sheet.
- It also requires coverage (the top cause, one numeric piece of evidence, the next measurement), so vague text cannot pass.
- The model gets one rewrite; after that a fixed template is used.
- Scripted mode (templates only, no generated text) is the default for every lesson.
technical_components.novelty_vs_prior_art: Motivated by measured error rates of LLM lab assistants: more than 1 in 10 answers harmful (Kregear et al. 2025), and about 20% of feedback containing errors (Maus et al. 2025). Grounded generation plus checking is common. A physics fact-sheet verifier for lab feedback, validated against a blinded audit, was not found.
technical_components.feasibility_and_memory: The verifier runs in milliseconds on the CPU. 4B generation takes a few seconds (estimate).

technical_components.name: Product integration, local serving and memory watchdog
technical_components.novelty_vs_prior_art: Engineering. It removes the external GLM dependency and makes the offline booth possible.
technical_components.feasibility_and_memory: Estimate 5.5-8 GB for the whole product, to be measured on 11-09. The assistants write the UI code 11-04..11-08; before 11-06 it is launched only briefly, with the owner's OK.

technical_components.name: Adapter deployment path and parity gate
technical_components.what:
- PEFT-to-mlx-vlm converter: renames keys; transposes PEFT lora_A (r, in) to lora_a (in, r) and lora_B (out, r) to lora_b (r, out); sets scale = alpha/r. Before 11-06 it passes a round-trip test on tiny random tensors and a name-map test.
- Serving: mlx_vlm.server --adapter-path on lmstudio-community Qwen3.5-4B-MLX-4bit, reusing the folder lms downloaded, so there are no duplicate copies.
- Gate: a 200-case parity test (>= 95% identical top-1) plus the adapter-effect check.
- Fallbacks:
  - mlx-vlm's dequantise-add-requantise fuse into the 4-bit model (never mlx_lm.fuse, which drops the vision tower);
  - Mac-native mlx-vlm SFT from engine traces;
  - ship v1 with the untuned 4B plus the engine, and swap the adapter in at v1.1.
technical_components.novelty_vs_prior_art: Engineering. LM Studio cannot load LoRA adapters, so without this path the upgrade could not run on a school laptop.
technical_components.feasibility_and_memory: The adapter is about 65 MB, about 11 minutes even at 100 KB/s. The converter is about 150 lines (estimate), written 11-04.

technical_components.name: Real fault-injection kit (student researcher only)
technical_components.what:
- Experiments: 3, chosen by kit availability among Hooke's law, friction and Newton-2. Newton-2 is used only if a photogate or ticker timer exists; otherwise average speed with a distance-reference fault replaces it.
- Conditions: clean plus 3 causes per experiment, x 2 repeats. A seeded random schedule is committed with its hash before each session, and the student draws the conditions himself on sealed cards.
- Each experiment includes at least one cause pair that the atlas predicts the standard worksheet confounds.
- Data are typed into CSV and frozen (hashed) before any software sees them.
- Every run continues with BOTH the EIG follow-up and a repeat, in a committed random order.
- The kit also measures the vertical-to-horizontal zero shift of the school's spring scales and, on >= 6 runs, the fix-and-verify prediction.
- No photos, no names and no other person's data. No condition manipulates or measures the student's own reaction time; timing faults are simulated only.
technical_components.novelty_vs_prior_art: Fault injection is a classic validation method. Using it to validate an AI lab diagnoser and an EIG advisor on real school apparatus was not found.
technical_components.feasibility_and_memory: About 10-15 min per run (estimate); 24 runs over two sessions. Form 3 covers falling masses, springs and carts, with safety glasses.

technical_components.name: Open-set recognition: rules first, Set-of-Mark VLM fallback, one question, candidate sets, minimal pairs
technical_components.novelty_vs_prior_art: Open-set recognition, conformal prediction for zero-shot VLMs (Silva-Rodriguez et al., CVPR 2025), clarification under ambiguity (CLAM) and minimal-pair tests (Winoground, MMVP, NaturalBench) all exist. Not found: set-valued experiment recognition with one clarifying question, and equipment-level minimal pairs with matched-artifact controls.
technical_components.feasibility_and_memory:
- Inference only.
- Estimate a few seconds per image on the 4B, and about 20 s per image for the 27B baseline in an overnight batch with nothing else loaded.
- Built by the second assistant from 11-06.
- The in-domain data are few and clustered: 3 source videos, a few photo sessions, no in-domain Hooke photos. Hence P1, with honest small-n statistics.

technical_components.name: Judge Challenge, practice mode and teacher protocol view
technical_components.what:
- Booth: 12 paper sabotage cards (no QR codes or URLs). The judge picks a card and a fault size, the hi-fi simulator generates the table, and the app must name the culprit within <= 3 extra measurements, offline on the 4B tier. Precomputed scenarios are the fallback.
- The same code provides a practice mode for ordinary teaching (find a planted fault with the fewest measurements) and the teacher's assessment mode (evidence shown, verdict hidden).
- Protocol view: the atlas heat map for today's worksheet, plus the one protocol change that fixes most confounds.
technical_components.novelty_vs_prior_art: Product framing. Tracker overlays a model someone builds by hand, and PhET simulates ideal worlds; neither infers the fault behind a student's own data.
technical_components.feasibility_and_memory: Reuses labsim, the engine and the UI; negligible memory. Built only after P0 is complete, and cut first if time runs short.

technical_components.name: Later phases written into the plan now (nothing can be added after the affiliated fair)
technical_components.novelty_vs_prior_art: Adds scale, vision-side and field evidence; no new method.
technical_components.feasibility_and_memory: Each phase is listed with the same methods and metrics, so later data collection stays within the approved plan.

design.model_upgrade:
WHAT IS MODIFIED
The language side of Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B. It is an official Apache-2.0 vision-language model with native image and video input. It uses the same qwen3_5 hybrid architecture (Gated DeltaNet + gated attention) as the student's Qwen3.8-27B, and its MLX 4-bit build is 3.06 GB.
- Adapter: bf16 LoRA, r=16, alpha=32, dropout 0.05, on language-model linear layers whose PEFT names map one-to-one to mlx-vlm's qwen3_5 modules.
- Full-attention q/k/v/o and MLP gate/up/down come first. The Gated-DeltaNet projections are added only if the converter's name-map test passes, because vLLM packs some of them (in_proj_qkv with in_proj_z, in_proj_b with in_proj_a).
- Frozen: vision tower, embeddings, lm_head. Non-thinking chat format; loss on assistant tokens only.
- Adapter size about 65 MB (estimate).

SKILL TAUGHT
Input:
- an experiment card: the law in linearised form, variables, units and instrument resolutions;
- candidate causes written as plain physical descriptions, with no signature tags, plus 'random error only';
- the data table (1-8 rows);
- the code-computed signature panel;
- a menu of 3-6 feasible extra measurements.
Output, in a fixed JSON schema:
- short evidence and the data's signature;
- for each cause, its predicted signature type and probability;
- p(none of these);
- the most informative next measurement, with the expected result under the top two causes;
- the z verdict;
- an explanation of <= 80 words in Chinese or English.
In 20% of examples the cause list is withheld, and the model proposes up to 6 causes as (variable, signature type, description).

DATA SOURCE
- About 20,000 prompts; the final count is set by measured throughput.
- Generated on the rented GPU server by seeded labsim code, from the six curriculum experiments only.
- Labelled by the Bayesian engine: the posterior rounded to 0.05, the argmax-EIG menu item, each cause's signature tag, and a templated bilingual explanation.
- One cause per curriculum experiment, and all six held-out experiments, never appear in training.
- No human labels, no frontier-API outputs, no student data. Only code is uploaded.

TRAINING
- S1, engine-target SFT (P0, the primary arm): one time-boxed run (<= 2 h or 2 epochs) with one pre-specified checkpoint.
- Shuffled-label control (P0): the same prompts, steps and seed, with cause labels permuted within each experiment.
- S2, expert iteration (P1): sample 8 answers per prompt from the merged S1 model on about 3k fresh training prompts. Keep the best one if reward R >= a pre-registered threshold, where R = format gate x (0.5 x (1 - 0.5 x ||p - q||^2) + 0.3 x EIG(chosen)/max EIG + 0.2 x verifier pass with coverage) and q is the engine posterior. Then train one SFT epoch continuing from S1.
- S3, GRPO on the same reward (P2): only if the GPU is idle before 11-10; otherwise Phase 2.
- Tooling: Unsloth, falling back to ms-swift, then plain PEFT/TRL.
- Weights, thresholds, step counts and the deployment rule are committed before training.

COMPUTE LOCATION
- Rented RTX 5090 (32 GB). bf16 LoRA of the 4B needs about 10 GB VRAM per Unsloth's Qwen3.5 table. The table does not state a sequence length, so this is verified in the first run. Training in bf16 avoids Unsloth's warning against QLoRA for this family.
- The environment is set up on 11-06 with no data: PyTorch for CUDA >= 12.8 (needed for sm_120), transformers >= 5.2, flash-linear-attention and causal-conv1d.
- Evaluation and S2 sampling serve merged models with vLLM's qwen3_5 class (its LoRA support is unconfirmed), falling back to batched HF generate.
- Throughput is measured in each job's first 10 minutes, and every job is time-boxed.
- If the stack fails, a reduced S1 is trained overnight on the Mac with mlx-vlm (estimate 6-10 GB, nothing else loaded).

DEPLOYMENT PATH
1. The adapter (about 65 MB) goes to the Mac via a private Hugging Face repo or direct download.
2. A PEFT-to-MLX converter renames keys, transposes lora_A/lora_B and sets scale = alpha/r.
3. mlx_vlm.server --adapter-path serves it on lmstudio-community Qwen3.5-4B-MLX-4bit, with JSON schema, token logprobs and thinking off by default. This server is needed because LM Studio cannot load adapters.
4. A 200-case parity gate (>= 95% identical top-1) and the adapter-effect check must pass.
Fallbacks: mlx-vlm's dequantise-add-requantise fuse into the 4-bit model (never mlx_lm.fuse, which drops the vision tower); or ship v1 with the untuned 4B plus the engine and swap the adapter in at v1.1.
In the product, the engine supplies the probabilities for the six curriculum experiments and the tuned model writes checked explanations. For any other experiment, the tuned model's diagnosis is shown, labelled 'AI estimate'.

HOW IT IS MEASURED
- Primary (C3): top-1 cause accuracy on 720 held-out-experiment cases, S1 vs the untuned 4B, exact McNemar, also reported as a fraction of the Bayes-optimal oracle. It counts only if the shuffled-label control gains < 2 pp.
- Ladder (secondary, Holm): in-distribution, noise-shift, withheld-cause, hi-fi misspecified world, and near- vs far-transfer held-out experiments. Also S2 vs S1, EIG-regret, Brier/ECE, per-cause signature accuracy, recall@6 of proposed causes, faithfulness, and non-inferiority to the untuned 27B.
- References, all under the identical contract: engine and oracle; GBT and the rule matcher with oracle tags; the 3-shot in-context base; no-panel ablations; two frontier APIs.
- Must not change (TOST): photo recognition within +/-5 pp; PhyX-300 within +/-3 pp.
- Deployment: Mac/server parity, memory and latency.
- Stated in advance as 'no upgrade': S1 not better than base on the held-out experiments, or better only in-distribution.

WHY THE 4B, NOT THE 27B
- bf16 LoRA of the 27B needs about 56 GB, more than the card's 32 GB.
- Unsloth advises against QLoRA for Qwen3.5, and a bnb-4bit-trained adapter on the MLX affine 4-bit base is untested.
- The 27B alone already takes 18.5-21 GB of the 24 GB cap, so it cannot run beside the app.
- The 4B fits 8 GB school laptops.
The 27B stays the zero-shot generalist that the 4B specialist is compared against on the same Mac.

CONSIDERED AND NOT ADOPTED
- Counterfactual vision tuning on the 809 images (only 3 source videos); moved to Phase 2.
- The 24-family simulator.
- 9B GRPO as the headline.
- Distilling an API teacher.
- 27B QLoRA.
- Letting the VLM read gauges (MeasureBench: the best model reaches 30.3% on real images), so readings stay manual.

experiments.name: E1 Identifiability atlas (tests C1)
experiments.data: labsim with literature-calibrated noise for the 6 curriculum and 6 held-out experiments. The fault library is frozen by hash after the student's review.
experiments.arms_and_baselines:
- Protocols: P0 single reading (old app); P1 standard worksheet; P1 + 1 EIG measurement; P1 + 2 EIG measurements.
- Controls: P1 + 1 repeat; P1 + 1 random menu item.
- Sensitivity, for the curriculum experiments: fault-size priors x0.5 and x2; noise x0.5 and x2.
experiments.metrics_and_stats:
- Bayes-optimal top-1 accuracy (MAP under the true generative model) with Wilson 95% CIs.
- Full confusion matrices.
- Pairwise Bayes accuracy, and the list of robustly confounded pairs (< [0.6] in every sensitivity setting).
- For each confounded pair: the resolving measurement and its pairwise accuracy.
- Protocol differences by paired bootstrap on the same simulated cases.
experiments.sample_size: 500 simulated datasets per experiment x protocol cell, and 300 per cause pair (Wilson half-width about +/-4.4 pp at 0.5). Estimate 1-3 CPU-hours with 4 workers.
experiments.human_participants_status: None; purely computational.

experiments.name: E2 Engine validity, calibration and honesty
experiments.arms_and_baselines:
- The old app: relative error < 15% means verified; it cannot name causes.
- A rule checklist (intercept sign, curvature, ratio < 1), written before seeing test data.
- The engine with literature noise.
- The oracle with the true generating parameters.
experiments.metrics_and_stats:
- Top-1 and top-3 accuracy, macro-F1.
- False-alarm rate on clean data.
- 'Not in my list' rate and AUROC on unmodelled cases.
- Brier score, log score, ECE with reliability diagrams.
- Exact McNemar for engine vs checklist.
- Degradation under noise shift and in the hi-fi world, with paired bootstrap CIs.
- Ratio of simulated to published spread, with a bootstrap CI.
experiments.sample_size: 2,250 cases; seconds to minutes of CPU.
experiments.human_participants_status: None.

experiments.name: E3 Simulated closed loop (tests C2a)
experiments.data: 840 cases: 600 in-distribution and 240 from held-out experiments. Each is continued with extra measurements generated by the hi-fi simulator, and again by labsim as an in-model check.
experiments.arms_and_baselines:
- EIG.
- EIG per lab minute.
- Repeat the last measurement (students' usual default).
- A random menu item.
- A fixed textbook protocol extension.
experiments.metrics_and_stats:
- Primary for C2a: the engine posterior of the true cause after one extra measurement, EIG vs repeat, paired Wilcoxon signed-rank.
- Secondary: posterior after two extra measurements; top-1 after 1 and 2 (exact McNemar); measurements needed to reach posterior 0.9 (Kaplan-Meier, log-rank).
- Holm correction across the non-primary strategy comparisons.
experiments.sample_size: 840 cases x 5 strategies, paired, in two worlds.
experiments.human_participants_status: None.

experiments.name: E4 Model upgrade and transfer ladder (tests C3, the primary; secondaries S-a to S-h)
experiments.arms_and_baselines:
- References: the engine (Bayes-optimal under our assumptions) and the oracle; gradient-boosted trees on panel features plus oracle cause tags; the 20-line rule matcher plus oracle tags.
- Qwen3.5-4B untuned, both zero-shot and with 3 in-context examples drawn from training experiments.
- 4B-S1 (primary); 4B-S2 (P1); 4B-S3 (P2).
- 4B shuffled-label LoRA (negative control).
- No-panel ablations of base and S1.
- Qwen3.8-27B untuned, non-thinking: the deployed MLX 4-bit build on the Mac, run overnight alone on a stratified 800-case subset (360 of them held-out).
- Two frontier API models, precomputed on 600 stratified synthetic cases each, with the same contract and schema via structured outputs; model versions and dates logged; schema failures count as wrong.
- Every arm gets the identical prompt contract, inputs, schema, greedy decoding and 512-token budget.
experiments.sample_size:
- About 3,800 cases per server-side 4B arm, run in bf16 and batched; well under 1 h per arm (estimate).
- Power estimate: 720 paired cases at about 22% discordance give about 0.8 power for a 5-pp difference (normal approximation).
- The 27B subset (800 cases at an estimated 30-40 s each) takes about one night.
- API arms: 600 cases each.
experiments.human_participants_status: None; simulator data only.

experiments.name: E5 Real closed-loop validation on the student's own apparatus (tests C2b)
experiments.data:
The student's own measurements on school apparatus; no photos.
- 3 experiments x 4 conditions x 2 repeats = 24 runs. The conditions are clean plus 3 causes, including at least one pair the atlas says the worksheet confounds.
- Each run is followed by BOTH the EIG measurement and a repeat, in a committed random order (48 follow-ups).
- Also: the spring-scale zero shift (>= 10 readings per scale, >= 3 scales), and fix-and-verify on >= 6 runs.
- Phase 2 extends toward about 60 runs with the same method.
experiments.arms_and_baselines:
- Engine.
- 4B-S1 (or S2 if shipped).
- 4B base.
- 27B (batch).
- The old app.
- The rule checklist.
- Within each run: the EIG follow-up vs the repeat follow-up.
experiments.metrics_and_stats:
- C2b: gain in the engine posterior of the sealed cause, EIG vs repeat, paired Wilcoxon.
- Top-1 against the sealed condition, before vs after the extra measurement (exact McNemar).
- Wilson CIs per arm; false alarms on clean runs.
- Simulator realism: residual scatter against literature noise (chi^2/dof).
- Spring-scale zero shift as mean +/- SD; fix-and-verify agreement.
experiments.sample_size: 24 runs plus 48 follow-ups (estimate 4-6 h over two sessions). Power estimate: 24 paired runs detect a standardised effect of about 0.6 (Wilcoxon, alpha 0.05, power 0.8). Wide CIs are reported; for example, 18/24 correct gives about 55-88%.

experiments.name: E6 Explanation faithfulness and verifier validity (tests S-f)
experiments.data: Explanations from every arm in E4 and E5. A stratified, blinded sample of 150 for the student's own audit (arm labels hidden; about 2 h).
experiments.arms_and_baselines:
- 4B base.
- 4B-S1/S2.
- 27B zero-shot.
- 27B given the engine fact sheet (an explain-only reference, P1).
- API arms.
- Templates.
Each is run with and without the verifier gate.
experiments.metrics_and_stats:
- Verifier-flagged unsupported or wrong claims per explanation.
- Rewrite and template-fallback rates; coverage.
- Verifier precision and recall against the blinded audit, with Wilson CIs.
- Arm comparisons by exact McNemar with Holm.
- Stated limitation: the rater is the researcher.
experiments.sample_size: Several thousand explanations checked automatically; 150 audited by hand.
experiments.human_participants_status: None: the student researcher is the only rater. Ratings by teachers or classmates would be human-participant data and are excluded.

experiments.name: E7 Recognition (P1) and what-must-not-change checks (TOST)
experiments.data:
- Images from the 809-image annotated set that pass person screening and provenance clearance, grouped by source (3 video sources; photo sessions split by EXIF time).
- 150-300 external CC BY / CC BY-SA images and keyframes (Commons stills, Getaclass, Physics Wikiexperiments), with a licence manifest and labels verified by the student.
- 150-250 minimal pairs with matched-artifact controls.
- 300 PhyX items (MIT licence).
experiments.arms_and_baselines:
- The current rule classifier.
- Rules plus the 'What will you measure?' question, with answers simulated from the ground-truth cue table.
- 4B base.
- 4B-S1 (the no-harm check; if it fails, a second base-model server handles recognition, adding about 3-4 GB).
- 27B, overnight batch, nothing else loaded.
- Two frontier APIs, on CC images only.
All use the same Set-of-Mark input at <= 1024 px and the same schema.
experiments.metrics_and_stats:
- Top-1 on registered experiments; tie-resolution rate.
- Unknown-experiment AUROC from letter logprobs.
- Split-conformal coverage and set size per source group (small-n; no guarantee claimed).
- Flip rate for decisive vs control masks (exact McNemar over image pairs).
- TOST: 4B-S1 vs base recognition within +/-[5] pp, and PhyX within +/-[3] pp (90% CI).
- Latency vs image size; cluster bootstrap by source.
experiments.sample_size:
- Estimate about 250 independent photos (if cleared), plus up to 3 video clusters sampled at 10 frames each.
- 150-300 CC images; 150-250 minimal pairs; 300 PhyX items.
- If the existing images are not cleared, E7 rests on the CC set alone.
experiments.human_participants_status: None, provided the images show apparatus only and their provenance is cleared. Public images are cited with their licences. Anything showing identifiable people is cropped, blurred or excluded.

experiments.name: E8 Engineering criteria on the Mac
experiments.data:
- Scripted sessions of 30 photos and 30 diagnoses with networking disabled.
- 200 parity cases.
- 50 timed runs per scenario.
experiments.arms_and_baselines:
- Product with the 4B and adapter vs product with the untuned 4B.
- The 27B alone, for the memory and latency comparison.
- Server bf16 adapter vs the Mac 4-bit build.
experiments.metrics_and_stats:
- Peak summed memory from the watchdog log, against the caps.
- Median and 90th-percentile latency per stage.
- Schema-valid rate.
- Offline pass/fail.
- Manual-selection checklist.
- Parity (top-1 agreement, Cohen's kappa) and the adapter-effect check.
experiments.sample_size: 60 interactions plus 200 parity cases; estimate 1-2 h.
experiments.human_participants_status: None; the student is the only tester.

experiments.name: E9 Conditional classroom study (Phase 3, IRB path, not before Dec 2026)
experiments.data: Collected only after a 3-member school IRB approves: students' written identification of error sources on a predict-observe-explain worksheet, with vs without the scripted Detective card. Data are group-level and de-identified by an adult.
experiments.arms_and_baselines: Scripted Detective card vs the same lesson without it, or a crossover over two lessons with different faults.
experiments.metrics_and_stats: A rubric the student adapts from published measurement-reasoning instruments that he finds and reads himself. Pre-registered group-level tests (McNemar, or rank tests) with Wilson CIs.
experiments.sample_size: Set in the IRB application (estimate: one or two classes). Small samples from one class threaten anonymity, so only aggregates are reported.

design.data_plan:
D1 SYNTHETIC (labsim; the primary data). Everything is generated by seeded code, and only code travels.
- Training pool, server only: about 20,000 prompts from the six curriculum experiments; the count is set by throughput.
  - Protocol mix: single reading, standard worksheet, and after one extra measurement.
  - Task mix: 20% cause-proposal tasks; 25% 'random error only'.
  - Chinese and English 50/50; cause IDs and order randomised; 3 paraphrases per text slot.
  - Labels: the engine posterior, the EIG of every menu item, the cause signature tags and the fact sheet.
- Withheld from training: one cause per curriculum experiment, and the six held-out experiments entirely.
